title: Stumbling corrective reaction during fictive locomotion in the cat.
notes: Stimulation of the cutaneous superficial peroneal nerve during the flexion phase of fictive locomotion in decerebrate cats reproduces the full stumbling corrective reaction — brief flexor excitation, flexor inhibition, recruitment of knee and ankle extensors, then post-stimulation flexor excitation with a prolonged flexion phase — showing the corrective synergy is assembled by spinal locomotor circuitry from short-latency cutaneous reflexes plus actions of the rhythm-generating network.

title: Significance of load receptor input during locomotion: a review
notes: Review making the case that extensor load receptors are central to locomotor control: in the cat, Golgi tendon organ input switches function during walking from Ib inhibition to extensor facilitation proportional to load, and in humans leg extensor activation during stance scales with body weight — one load-regulatory mechanism spanning quadrupedal and bipedal gait.

title: Cutaneous Reflexes During Human Gait: Electromyographic and Kinematic Responses to Electrical Stimulation
notes: Non-noxious electrical stimulation of the superficial peroneal and tibial nerves during human walking produces phase-modulated cutaneous reflexes in leg muscles and correlated kinematic corrections — superficial peroneal responses amount to a stumbling-corrective reaction during swing, while tibial responses smooth the swing leg and assist foot placement and weight acceptance at the start of stance.

title: Speed-dependent locomotor adjustments following staggered thoracic lateral hemisections in adult cats
notes: Staggered thoracic lateral hemisections in cats shift the ipsilesional hindlimb from stance/extensor dominance toward swing/flexor while the contralateral limb compensates with prolonged stance and reduced swing, and forelimbs take extra steps independent of speed or lesion side — lesion signatures that reorganized sensorimotor network models must reproduce.
animal_study: Combine the staggered hemisections with dorsal-root deafferentation to test how much of the ipsilesional swing/stance rebalancing and contralateral stance compensation depends on afferent feedback versus reorganized central circuits, across walking speeds.
robot_sim: Model staggered hemisection as unilateral loss of descending drive plus partial crossed-connection removal in a quadruped CPG; test whether ipsilesional stance shortening, contralateral stance prolongation, and extra forelimb steps emerge without retuning, and how they scale with speed.

title: Left–right coordination from simple to extreme conditions during split-belt locomotion in the chronic spinal adult cat
notes: These people make cat zombies

title: Biologically based distributed control and local reflexes improve rough terrain locomotion in a hexapod robot
A Synthetic Nervous System Controls a Simulated Cockroach
notes: Design-process paper for synthetic nervous systems: SimRoach2, a dynamical cockroach model with antagonistic Hill-muscle joints, is controlled by a distributed SNS built from insect-known plus hypothetical pathways, with each joint's controller tuned as a proportional-integral loop by local numerical optimization — reliable low-level locomotion without global optimization.

title: Adaptive control for backward quadrupedal walking. III. Stumbling corrective reactions and cutaneous reflex sensitivity.
notes: In cats walking forward or backward on a treadmill, paw taps that obstruct swing evoke direction-appropriate stumbling corrective reactions — draw the limb away from the obstacle, lift it over, then reposition for stance — while stance-phase taps leave the ongoing step largely unchanged but exaggerate the next swing; mechanical taps produce far richer responses than electrical pulses, so cutaneous reflex sensitivity is structured by phase, gait direction, and stimulus modality.

title: V1 and V2b Interneurons Secure the Alternating Flexor-Extensor Motor Activity Mice Require for Limbed Locomotion
notes: V1 and V2b interneurons together supply the inhibitory component that secures alternating flexor-extensor activity: removing V1/V2b-derived neurotransmission in the isolated mouse spinal cord synchronizes L2 flexor and L5 extensor rhythms, and mice lacking V1/V2b inhibition cannot articulate limb joints — identifying these two ventral inhibitory classes as core elements of the limb CPG.

title: Multisensory control of spinal reflex pathways.
Forelimb movements contribute to hindlimb cutaneous reflexes during locomotion in cats
notes: During quadrupedal locomotion in cats, forelimb movement modulates hindlimb cutaneous reflexes evoked by superficial peroneal stimulation, particularly the occurrence of long-latency responses — evidence that interlimb (forelimb-hindlimb) signals gate spinal cutaneous reflex pathways during walking.
animal_study: Externally drive forelimb movements in spinal-transected cats while stimulating the superficial peroneal nerve during hindlimb locomotion, testing whether the forelimb-dependent modulation of long-latency hindlimb reflexes survives transection and localizing the gating circuit.
robot_sim: Add forelimb-state-dependent gain modulation to hindlimb cutaneous reflex pathways in a quadruped neuromechanical model; ablating the modulation should remove the long-latency reflex gating present during quadrupedal walking.

title: A physiologically inspired hybrid CPG/Reflex controller for cycling simulations that generalizes to walking
notes: A hybrid controller pairing a Unit Burst Generator feedforward CPG with a small reflex set simulates physiological cycling across speeds and seat heights and transfers to walking after adding only a balance component, demonstrating that physiologically grounded CPG+reflex hybrids can generalize across cyclical lower-limb tasks instead of being task-specific.
animal_study: Perturb the crank or seat during human cycling and compare evoked reflex responses with the controller's feedback components, validating which reflex pathways are actually engaged in steady cycling and whether the same set carries over to walking.
robot_sim: Implement the Unit Burst Generator plus limited reflex set on a cycling musculoskeletal model; verify generalization across speeds and seat heights, ablate the reflex component to quantify its contribution, and add the balance module to test walking transfer.

title: Parallel Complementary Strategies for Implementing Biological Principles into Mobile Robots
notes: Two parallel robot lines — cockroach-mimicking multi-segmented legs versus abstracted one-motor-per-tripod platforms whose gait changes emerge from passive mechanisms — establish that preflexive biomechanics can implement terrain-adaptive gait switching without neural control, capturing biological locomotion principles in deployable hardware.
animal_study: Test how much of the cockroach's terrain-dependent gait change survives neural silencing (anesthetized or nerve-cut preparations moving over obstacles), quantifying the preflexive-mechanical contribution that the passive robot designs posit.
robot_sim: Build an abstracted hexapod with passive gait-change mechanisms; lock or remove the passive degrees of freedom to measure how much terrain adaptation survives without them, isolating preflexive from neurally controlled contributions.

title: Mechanisms of adaptive interlimb coordination to sudden ground loss: a neuromusculoskeletal modeling study
notes: A neuromusculoskeletal cat model with two-level half-center CPGs per hindlimb reproduces the adaptive interlimb coordination observed when spinalized cats suddenly lose ground support — without any parameter re-optimization — and nullcline analysis attributes the robustness to afferent feedback controlling the transitions between fast and slow neuronal dynamics.
animal_study: In spinalized cats trained to walk, deliver sudden ground-loss perturbations while selectively suppressing group I afferent conduction, testing the prediction that afferent control of fast-slow transitions — not re-tuned parameters — carries the adaptive interlimb response.
robot_sim: Implement paired two-level half-center CPGs whose fast-slow transitions are controlled by afferent feedback, tuned on flat ground only; drop the foot into a hole without re-optimization and check that adaptive interlimb coordination emerges, then analyze the transition nullclines.

title: V3 spinal neurons establish a robust and balanced locomotor rhythm during walking.
notes: Blocking neurotransmission from excitatory V3 neurons (tetanus toxin) or acutely reducing their excitability destabilizes the locomotor rhythm, and V3 activity balances output between the two halves of the spinal cord — V3 neurons distribute excitatory drive bilaterally to keep the walking rhythm robust and left-right symmetric.
animal_study: Unilateral V3 silencing would directly test the proposed bilateral drive distribution, predicting left-right rhythm asymmetry or compensatory contralateral changes that bilateral blockade cannot resolve.
robot_sim: Add a bilaterally projecting excitatory V3-analog population distributing drive between the two half-centers; ablating it should produce an irregular, unbalanced rhythm without abolishing locomotion entirely.

title: Contribution of Sensory Feedback to the Generation of Extensor Activity During Walking in the Decerebrate Cat
notes: Letting the foot step into a hole reduces knee and ankle extensor activity to roughly 70% of normal in decerebrate cats, and selectively resisting ankle extension restores it; with segmental dorsal-root sections mapped accordingly, more than half of stance-phase extensor drive is proprioceptive — a continuous load-scaled contribution that automatically matches burst intensity to external demands.
animal_study: Selective inactivation of spindles versus tendon organs during stance (vibration, local anesthetic) combined with foot-in-hole trials would identify which proprioceptor class supplies the load-dependent extensor burst reinforcement.
robot_sim: Implement autogenic load-dependent extensor burst reinforcement during stance in a neuromechanical walker; removing ground support should cut extensor activity to about 70%, and resisting extension should restore it, directly testing the afferent share of stance drive.

title: A genetically defined asymmetry underlies the inhibitory control of flexor–extensor locomotor movements
notes: V1 and V2b inhibitory interneurons act in opposition on flexor-extensor alternation: V1 ablation causes limb hyperflexion (V1-derived inhibition is needed for proper extension), while V2b loss causes hindlimb hyperextension and delays the stance-to-swing transition, with each class biased toward innervating flexor- versus extensor-related motoneurons.
animal_study: Combine V1 or V2b ablation with deafferentation to test whether the hyperflexion/hyperextension and the delayed stance-to-swing transition persist without sensory input, separating inhibitory gating deficits from afferent compensation.
robot_sim: Model V1 and V2b inhibitory populations with biased flexor/extensor motoneuron innervation; ablating V2b should reproduce hyperextension plus a delayed stance-to-swing transition, and ablating V1 hyperflexion.

title: Adaptive control for backward quadrupedal walking. II. Hindlimb muscle synergies
notes: Backward walking in cats reuses the forward reciprocal synergies — flexors in swing, extensors in stance — but retunes temporal parameters and amplitudes (gastrocnemius active from midswing with ramping stance EMG, near-absent knee and ankle yield, early-ending iliopsoas with prolonged semitendinosus), indicating one direction-general circuit with task-specific reweighting.
animal_study: Load and unload extensors during backward walking (as done for forward) or deafferent trained cats walking backward to quantify how much of the re-timed synergies depends on afferent feedback versus central reweighting.
robot_sim: Retune only burst timing and amplitude parameters of a single CPG-synergy controller to reproduce backward-walking EMG benchmarks (LG from midswing, ramping stance EMG, absent yield), testing whether one synergy set covers both directions with temporal reweighting alone.

title: The special nature of human walking and its neural control
notes:
Review paper. 
Walking the way we do is inherently unstable. Sophisticated neurological control systems are required to ensure that we progress and maintain our balance at the same time. Most of what is known about the functional organization of these neurological control systems is inferred from studies on animals. Here, I compare selected studies on the neural control of human walking with similar studies in reduced animal preparations. The simple monosynaptic reflex appears to be controlled by comparable mechanisms in walking cats and humans. However, peripheral feedback mechanisms suggested to contribute to the switch from stance to swing on the basis of experiments in reduced cat preparations have little influence during human walking. A cat whose spinal cord has been completely transected can be made to walk on a treadmill by drug injections, but such an immediate effect of pharmacological intervention is not seen in humans. However, there have been reports that pharmacological intervention can improve the walking of patients with incomplete spinal cord injury, especially when pharmacological treatment is combined with training.

title: Fundamental contributions of the cat model to the neural control of locomotion
Function of Segmental Reflexes in the Control of Stepping in Cockroaches and Cats
Frequency-dependent recruitment of V2a interneurons during fictive locomotion in the mouse spinal cord
notes: V2a interneurons are dispensable for left-right coordination at low locomotor frequencies but essential at high frequencies because rhythmic synaptic drive to a subpopulation grows with cycle frequency and recruits subthreshold oscillating V2a neurons — speed-dependent recruitment within one pool rather than activation of a silent second set.
animal_study: Record identified V2a neurons in vivo across treadmill speeds to confirm the frequency-dependent recruitment seen in vitro, and test whether left-right coordination errors at high gait speeds correlate with V2a recruitment failure.
robot_sim: Model a V2a pool whose subthreshold units recruit as rhythmic synaptic drive grows with cycle frequency; ablating it should degrade left-right coordination only at high frequencies while sparing low-frequency alternation.

title: Whisker Deafferentation and Rodent Whisking Patterns: Behavioral Evidence for a Central Pattern Generator
notes: Bilateral infraorbital nerve section in head-fixed rats leaves the generation, patterning, and bilateral coordination of whisking intact, meeting the strict sensory-independence criteria for a whisking central pattern generator; unilateral section produces only a transient bilateral increase in whisking frequency.
animal_study: Locate the whisking CPG with serial transections combined with kinematic recording, or test pattern modulation after partial deafferentation using natural reafferent perturbations such as air puffs on the whiskers.
robot_sim: Remove all sensory feedback from a bilateral rhythmic model and verify that generation, patterning, and bilateral coordination persist — the deafferentation benchmark for CPG claims — and add a transient frequency elevation after unilateral feedback loss to match the behavioral result.

title: ScaFi: Length-Scalable, Compliant, Parametric Robotic Fish Design for Operation in Multiple Environmental Niches
notes: We demonstrate the scalability of the design in three physical pro totypes that span lengths from 50 cm to over 2.5 meters.

title: Made-to-order spiking neuron model equipped with a multi-timescale adaptive threshold
notes: A spiking neuron model combining a nonresetting leaky integrator with a multi-timescale adaptive threshold reproduces and predicts diverse spike responses — regular spiking, intrinsic bursting, fast spiking, and chattering — with only three adaptive threshold parameters, expressing firing characteristics as a continuum rather than discrete classes at low computational cost.
animal_study: Fit the three adaptive-threshold parameters to intracellular recordings of identified spinal interneurons and validate predicted responses to fluctuating current injection, testing the made-to-order claim on locomotor rather than cortical neurons.
robot_sim: Use the multi-timescale adaptive-threshold IF unit as a low-cost spiking neuron class in CPG networks; sweep its three parameters across regular-spiking to intrinsic-bursting regimes and measure how heterogeneous unit classes influence network rhythm properties.

title: Embryonic assembly of a central pattern generator without sensory input
notes: The Drosophila peristaltic-crawling circuitry assembles into a functional central pattern generator with no sensory input at all, but sensory information is required to integrate the circuit into actual locomotion: without afferent input, movement polarity is deranged and backward peristaltic waves predominate at the expense of forward peristalsis.
animal_study: Restore individual sensory modalities in sensory-null embryos (class-specific mechanoreceptor rescue) to determine which afferent inputs re-establish forward-polarity peristalsis, identifying the polarity-determining sensory signal.
robot_sim: Assemble a peristaltic-crawling CPG with zero afferent feedback and verify the rhythm self-organizes; then add sensory feedback to control wave polarity, ablating it to reproduce the backward-dominant peristalsis seen without afferents.

title: Motor circuits in action: specification, connectivity, and function
notes: Review of motor circuit assembly: specification, connectivity, and function of spinal motor circuits with a developmental-genetic lens.

title: Comparative Locomotor Systems
notes: Comparative synthesis arguing that basic principles of locomotor network organization are conserved between vertebrates and invertebrates, permitting mechanistic study at multiple physiological levels; sensory signals and neuromodulatory input reconfigure network properties, and these networks reorganize in response to nervous-system injury.
animal_study: Test the conserved-principles claim directly: apply the same phase-specific afferent stimulation or neuromodulatory perturbation to locomotor networks in one vertebrate and one invertebrate preparation and compare the network-level reconfiguration.
robot_sim: Implement CPG networks whose properties are reconfigurable by simulated neuromodulatory and sensory inputs, then reproduce the reported reorganization after simulated injury (partial deafferentation or transection) as a benchmark for recovery mechanisms.

title: Proprioceptive input resets central locomotor rhythm in the spinal cat.
notes:
Extensor group I afferents have access to central rhythm generators
 >Important in reflex regulation of stepping.


Rythm generators came mainly from Golgi Tendon Organ Ib afferents for group I

Increased load of limb extensor during the stance phase enhance and prolong extensor activity while simultaneously delaying the transition to the swing phase of the step cycle.

title: Learning CPG-based Biped Locomotion with a Policy Gradient Method: Application to a Humanoid Robot
notes: Computational model study. Our goals in this study are to achieve CPG-based biped walking with a 3D hardware humanoid and to develop an efficient learning algorithm with CPG by reducing the dimensional- ity of the state space used for learning.

title: Spatiotemporal activation of lumbosacral motoneurons in the locomotor step cycle
notes: A 3-D digital reconstruction of 27 cat hindlimb motoneuron pools, modulated by compiled EMG profiles, reveals a rostrocaudal oscillation of spinal activity across the step cycle: the caudal third of the lumbosacral enlargement dominates during stance, activation shifts abruptly rostral during swing, and a transient caudal focus at the stance-swing transition coincides with retractor muscles (gracilis, posterior biceps, semimembranosus, semitendinosus) that clear the foot from the ground.
animal_study: Run the designed follow-up: characterize the same spatiotemporal MN activation in a spinalized, deafferented preparation (no descending or sensory inputs) and compare with the intact pattern to isolate the CPG-internal spatiotemporal structure.
robot_sim: Distribute a simulated cat-scale MN pool model rostrocaudally per these digitized coordinates and phase-modulate the pools with EMG-derived profiles; test whether the rostrocaudal oscillation and the caudal stance-swing transition focus emerge, and how they degrade when sensory inputs are ablated.

title: Renshaw cell activity and recurrent effects on motoneurons during fictive locomotion.
notes: During fictive locomotion in pre- and post-mammillary cats, Renshaw cells fire rhythmic bursts tied to single phases of the step cycle, and recurrent inhibitory IPSPs persist in motoneurons through all phases with amplitudes inversely correlated with motoneuron membrane potential — evidence that recurrent inhibition is phase-structured within the locomotor pattern rather than a static gain setting.

title: Confluence of Active and Passive Control Mechanisms Enabling Autonomy and Terrain Adaptability for Robots in Variable Environments
notes: The CASE/NPS Beach Whegs robot demonstrates abstracted biological inspiration in practice: terrain-adaptive gaits emerge passively from insect-inspired mechanics, so the robot carries no gait sensors and its controller only issues speed and heading directives — evidence that morphological computation can replace explicit terrain-feedback control.
animal_study: Test the passive-adaptation claim on rapid-running insects: run them across graded heterogeneous terrain after disruption of leg afferent input and quantify how much terrain adaptation survives, separating preflexive mechanics from active sensory control.
robot_sim: Replicate the design principle in simulation: a legged model whose passive mechanics adapt gait to terrain with all gait sensors ablated, mapping which terrain classes are handled purely preflexively and where active control becomes necessary.

title: Activity of interneurons within the L4 spinal segment of the cat during brainstem-evoked fictive locomotion
notes: During MLR-evoked fictive locomotion in the decerebrate cat, midlumbar (L4) interneurons receiving group II input from quadriceps, sartorius, and pretibial flexors — and projecting to L7 motor nuclei — fired predominantly with ipsilateral flexor bursts and were less responsive to peripheral input during extension: a phase-gated group II pathway positioned to shape flexor activity.
animal_study: Test the pathway's causal role by reversibly silencing the identified L4 interneurons, or their group II input, during fictive locomotion and measuring changes in flexor burst timing and in the phase gating of peripheral responsiveness.
robot_sim: Implement a midlumbar interneuron layer receiving group II afferent input from quadriceps, sartorius, and pretibial flexor pathways and projecting to motor nuclei, with gain reduced during extension; test its contribution to flexor burst generation in a CPG model.

title: Neuromechanics: an integrative approach for understanding motor control.
notes: Manifesto for neuromechanics: understanding motor control requires the integrated nervous-system-plus-body as the unit of analysis; the intellectual case with examples across locomotion and feeding.

title: Sensory reweighting dynamics in human postural control
notes: Previous studies found that the contribution of each of these sensory systems changes depending on perturbations applied during stance and on environmental conditions.

title: Asymmetric control of cycle period by the spinal locomotor rhythm generator in the adult cat.
notes: In decerebrate and spinal cats, fictive locomotor cycle period varied predominantly with the extension phase while the flexion phase stayed relatively invariant; this walking-speed asymmetry (stance varies, swing constant) persisted without phasic sensory feedback, supraspinal structures, pharmacology, or sustained stimulation, establishing it as an intrinsic property of spinal CPG organization.
animal_study: Quantify how extraneous factors reshape the intrinsic asymmetry: apply phasic afferent stimulation, monoaminergic drugs, or sustained drive during fictive locomotion and measure whether dominance of extension-duration control shifts.
robot_sim: Build a half-center CPG whose cycle period is modulated primarily through extension (stance) duration with swing duration near-invariant; verify the asymmetry survives removal of all simulated sensory feedback, then add feedback to test modulation.

title: Kinesthetic Senses
notes: The kinesthetic senses are the senses of position and movement of the body, senses we are awareof only on introspection. A method used to study kinesthesia is muscle vibration, which engagesafferents of muscle spindles to trigger illusions of movement and changed position. When vibratingelbow ﬂexors, it generates sensations of forearm extension, when vibrating extensors, sensationsof forearm ﬂexion. Vibrating the elbow joint produces no illusion. Vibrating ﬂexors and extensorstogether at the same frequency also produces no illusion, because what is perceived is the signaldifference between antagonist muscles of each arm and between arms. The size of the illusiondepends on how the muscle has been conditioned beforehand, due to a property of muscle calledthixotropy. When measuring the illusion, blindfolded subjects may carry out a matching or pointingtask. In pointing, signals from muscle spindles are less important than in matching. Afferent signalsfrom kinesthetic receptors project to areas of somatosensory cortex to generate sensations ofdetection and location. This is referred to the body model, which provides information about sizeand shape of body parts. Kinesthesia, together with vision and touch, is associated with the senseof body ownership. All three can combine or each, on its own, can generate ownership

title: Central Pattern Generators of the Mammalian Spinal Cord
notes: Review of mammalian spinal central pattern generators emphasizing that one spinal cord produces multiple rhythmic behaviors — walking, running, swimming, scratching — each with its own goals and demands, and discussing how spinal circuitry is organized to deliver this complexity and flexibility.
animal_study: Test shared-versus-dedicated circuitry: record the same spinal interneurons during walking and scratching in the same animal to determine which elements are common across rhythmic behaviors and which are behavior-specific.
robot_sim: Implement a modular CPG architecture that recombines shared rhythm- and pattern-formation elements to generate multiple distinct rhythmic output sets, testing whether one network reproduces the different behaviors' demands.

title: Are muscle synergies useful for neural control?
notes: Computational model study. Finally, we showed that the number of synergies required to approximate the optimal muscle pattern for an arb.

title: Neural Control of Walking in People with Parkinsonism
notes: Review of neural control walking people parkinsonism. These impairments have been shown to be relatively independent (22, 41), and we postulate each depends on partially distinct neural networks.

title: Simulation of Human Balance Control Using an Inverted Pendulum Model
notes: A synthetic nervous system providing proportional-derivative control of a single-joint inverted pendulum model of human balance: an ankle angular-position sensor feeds a neural network that computes the derivative of position error and applies corrective torque about the ankle, maintaining unstable equilibrium and correcting perturbations — the minimal building block for larger neuromechanical balance controllers.

title: Spinal Cord Pattern Generators for Locomotion
notes:
CPG generates rhythm an shapes the pattern of bursts of motoneurons(Pg.2)

Cats with transected spinal cord and with cut dorsal roots still produce rhythmic alternating contraction in ankle flexors and extensors (Pg.2)

Basic mechanism underlying locomotion, no fundamental differences seems to exist between bipeds and quadrupeds.(Pg.2)

Differences between cats and primates may be due to increased importance of the Cortico spinal tract in primates. Additionally the gait of primates relies more on Supraspinal drive.(Pg.2)

Spinal Circuitry for locomotion might be suppressed by Supraspinal input, with the hypothesis be to free the movement of the hands and arms for locomotor movement.(Pg.3)

There are observation which indicate the neural controls of human locomotion is based on the activity of Spinal CPGs (Review Duysens and Van de Crommert,1998) (Pg. 3)

Selection of an appropriate locomotor pattern depends on a combination of CPGs and afferent inputs as well from the respective motor condition. This information is used to organize muscles synergies and meet multiple conditions of stance and gait (Review Mackay-Lyons,2002)(Pg. 3)

Backwards walking is seen to resemble the EMG-timings of hip muscles reversed in time as forward walking  (Pg. 3)

In humans powerful presynaptic inhibitory effects from flexor group 1 afferents onto extensor group 1 afferents exist, although are weak (Pg. 3)

Cortico-Spinal projections to lower limb motoneurons humans are stronger to the flexor tha

title: Neural control of rhythmic limb motion is shaped by size and speed
notes: Proposes a 'mechanics space' in which limb size and limb speed determine the dominant mechanical regime: inertia-dominated (large, fast limbs — muscle work becomes kinetic energy, requiring compensatory control and active damping), gravity/elastic-dominated (small, slow — compensatory control and active damping unnecessary), and viscous-dominated (small, fast — joint viscosity alone yields exclusively stable motion). Neural control strategy is thus set almost entirely by limb scale and speed.
animal_study: Test the framework's predictions across scale: perturb or partially disrupt active neural control in animals whose limbs fall in different mechanics-space regions and test whether stability losses occur only in the inertia-dominated regime.
robot_sim: Scale a limb model through the mechanics space and vary active damping and compensatory control accordingly; verify that stability persists without active control in the elastic and viscous regimes but is lost in the inertia regime without it.

title: Passive dynamics change leg mechanics for an unexpected surface during human hopping
notes: The goal of this study was to determine the contributions of anticipation and reaction when human hoppers encounter surprise, expected, and random changes from a soft elastic surface (27 kN/m) to a hard surface (411 kN/m).

title: The CPGs for Limbed Locomotion-Facts and Fiction.
notes: Review separating fact from fiction in limbed-locomotion CPG claims; takes a hard line on evidence quality for interneuronal and computational assertions.

title: Spinal circuitry of sensorimotor control of locomotion
notes: During locomotion many segmental hindlimb reflex pathways serve not only to regulate the excitability of local groups of motoneurones, but also to control the basic operation of the central pattern-generating circuitry responsible for locomotion. This is accomplished through a reorganization of reflexes that includes the suppression of reflex pathways operating at rest and the recruitment during locomotion of previously unrecognized types of spinal interneurones. In addition presynaptic inhibition of transmission from segmental afferents serves to regulate the gain of segmental reflexes and may contribute to the selection of particular reflex pathways during locomotion. The fictive locomotion preparation in adult decerebrate cats has proved to be an important tool in understanding reflex pathway reorganization. Further identification of the spinal interneurones involved in locomotor-dependent reflexes will contribute to our understanding not only of reflex pathway organization but also of the organization of the mammalian central pattern generator.

title: Probing the Human Spinal Locomotor Circuits by Phasic Step-Induced Feedback and by Tonic Electrical and Pharmacological Neuromodulation.
notes: Critical review arguing that rhythmic leg-muscle activity elicited in severe spinal cord injury by assisted treadmill stepping reflects entrainment of spinal proprioceptive reflex circuits by cyclically generated proprioceptive feedback rather than central pattern generator activation, and that genuine CPG engagement requires sustained tonic excitatory drive — from electrical spinal cord stimulation or combinations of dopaminergic, adrenergic, and 5-HT pharmacology.
animal_study: Dissociate the two mechanisms in a spinalized animal model: deliver tonic drive (epidural stimulation or monoamine agonists) and phasic limb movement independently and in combination, testing whether rhythmic output requires tonic drive while phasic feedback alone merely entrains reflex circuits.
robot_sim: Implement a lumbar circuit model with separately controlled reflex entrainment (cyclic proprioceptive input drives reflex circuits) and CPG activation (tonic excitatory drive gates rhythm generation); reproduce the dissociation and test rehabilitation-style combined stimulation.

title: Analyzing Modeled Torque Profiles to Understand Scale-Dependent Active Muscle Responses in the Hip Joint
notes: A multi-muscle biomechanical model analyzed across size scales shows that constituent hip torques (inertial, passive viscoelastic) shift in relative importance with animal size, predicting that extensor and flexor activation phases invert between small and large sizes executing the same kinematic motion — a scale-dependent principle for neural control strategy consistent with documented hindlimb torque during locomotion.
animal_study: Validate the predicted activation-phase inversion by recording hip extensor and flexor EMG in animals spanning large size scales performing matched kinematics, comparing observed phase relationships with the model's constituent-torque predictions.
robot_sim: Embed the scale-dependent torque analysis in a simulated multi-muscle limb: sweep size-scale, recompute the required extensor/flexor activation phasing, and verify the predicted phase flip and agreement with documented hindlimb torque profiles.

title: Synaptic actions on motoneurones caused by impulses in Golgi tendon organ afferents.
A Spinal Mechanism Related to Left–Right Symmetry Reduces Cutaneous Reflex Modulation Independently of Speed During Split-Belt Locomotion
notes: A spinal mechanism related to left-right symmetry reduces cutaneous reflex modulation independently of speed during split-belt locomotion — symmetry detection is a distinct spinal computation, not a speed by-product.

title: A simple model for clock-actuated legged locomotion
notes: The spring-loaded inverted pendulum alone cannot explain the dynamic stability of walking and running in many physically relevant parameter ranges; adding realistic hip-motor clock torques yields the clock-torqued CT-SLIP, which captures the robust stability observed in most animals and legged robots — feedforward clock-like actuation, not passive spring dynamics alone, underwrites gait stability.
animal_study: Test the model's implication in animals: measure stability boundaries under systematic parameter variation (speed, effective stiffness) and test whether CT-SLIP rather than passive SLIP predicts the observed robustness.
robot_sim: Implement CT-SLIP (a lossy SLIP with clock-torqued hip actuation) and map its stability properties against passive SLIP across parameter ranges, using it as the whole-body center-of-mass layer for legged locomotion controllers.

title: The role of cutaneous afferents from the distal hindlimb in the regulation of the step cycle of thalamic cats
notes: Cutaneous afferents from the distal hindlimb regulate the step cycle in thalamic cats: paw loading suppresses flexion during stance while stimulation can trigger and reset the cycle — load-related cutaneous feedback contributes to swing-stance transitions.

title: The comparative investigation of the stick insect and cockroach models in the study of insect locomotion
notes:
Highlights
•Stick insects and cockroaches have evolved to walk in very different environments.

•Common neural and biomechanical mechanisms facilitate comparative studies.

•Studies of both intact animals and reduced neural preparations have been instrumental.

•A common set of mathematical models enables research and comparison of key questions.

•Insights from insects inspire design of responsive, robust, and flexible bio-robots.

title: Integrative pattern of Ia synaptic actions on motoneurones of hip and knee muscles.
notes: Classic integrative map of Ia synaptic actions on hip and knee motoneurones: Ia excitation diverges broadly to synergists and across joints, fractionated into flexor and extensor recipient pools.

title: A dynamical model exploring sensory integration in the insect central complex substructures
notes: Dynamical model of sensory integration in insect central-complex substructures supporting navigation decisions.

title: The distal hindlimb musculature of the cat. Cutaneous reflexes during locomotion.
notes: Brief electrical stimulation of cutaneous nerves during cat treadmill locomotion evoked phase-gated short-latency reflexes — inhibition of extensors and excitation of flexors, expressed only during locomotor phases in which the respective motoneuron pools were active — while longer-latency components were gated similarly but not identically, indicating partial independence from the basic locomotor drive on the pool.
animal_study: Extend to fictive locomotion to test whether the phase-dependent gating of these cutaneous reflexes persists without movement-related afferent feedback, isolating central pattern control of reflex gain; and map additional distal nerves with the graphical gating technique.
robot_sim: Implement phase-gated cutaneous reflex pathways — flexor excitation and extensor inhibition enabled only during each pool's active locomotor phase, with separately gated late components — and test perturbation responses across the step cycle.

title: The Implications of Force Feedback for the λ Model
notes: In the λ-model framework, autogenic length feedback compensates muscle nonlinearities while positive force feedback — during level cat stepping largely restricted to gastrocnemius — reinforces the stiff ankle–knee linkage; heterogenic inhibitory force feedback spans different joints and axes, so it coordinates interjoint action and shifts activation thresholds, making threshold a feedback-dependent quantity rather than a pure descending control variable.

title: Modular organization of motor behavior in the frog's spinal cord
notes: First conceptualization of "motor primitives".

title: Operation of spinal sensorimotor circuits controlling phase durations during tied-belt and split-belt locomotion after a lateral thoracic hemisection
notes: Combining a computational model of cat locomotion with experiments shows that after thoracic lateral hemisection the contralesional ('intact') side remains governed mainly by supraspinal drives while the ipsilesional side is dominated by somatosensory feedback; simulations correctly predicted changes in cycle and phase durations during tied-belt and split-belt locomotion, and placing the ipsilesional hindlimb on the slow belt substantially reduced the effects of hemisection.
animal_study: Causally test the model's division of control by selectively deafferenting the ipsilesional hindlimb after hemisection (predicted loss of ipsilesional stepping), and by swapping belt-speed assignment to manipulate the slow-belt protective effect.
robot_sim: Simulate hemisection in a two-level CPG model by removing descending drive to one side; test whether ipsilesional stepping is sustained by somatosensory feedback alone, and reproduce the reduction of hemisection effects when the ipsilesional limb steps on the slow belt during split-belt locomotion.

title: Analyzing the Interplay Between Local CPG Activity and Sensory Signals for Inter-leg Coordination in Drosophila
notes: Tibia-amputated Drosophila legs show a speed-dependent stump oscillation — the wide range of possible periods at low walking speed collapses to a minimum as speed increases — which noisy leg CPGs stabilized by intra-leg load feedback and inter-leg coordinating signals can explain; the measured data anchor a simplified neuromuscular model of inter-leg coordination.

title: Reversal of the influence of group Ib afferents from plantaris on activity in medial gastrocnemius muscle during locomotor activity
notes: In clonidine-treated acute and chronic spinal cats, group I stimulation of the plantaris nerve entrained the locomotor rhythm and, during locomotor activity, group Ib afferents from plantaris exerted an excitatory action on medial gastrocnemius bursts (30-50 ms latency) through the extensor half-center of the rhythm generator — reversing the inhibitory effect the same stimuli produced on tonic activity without locomotion; selective Ia activation by muscle vibration neither entrained the rhythm nor augmented the bursts.
animal_study: Identify and reversibly inactivate the interneurons mediating the locomotor Ib reversal, then test extensor burst timing and rhythm entrainment under controlled plantaris loading across locomotor and non-locomotor states.
robot_sim: Implement state-dependent Ib feedback in a half-center CPG: autogenic inhibition at rest switching to excitation of the extensor half-center during locomotion, with rhythm entrainment by group I stimulation but not by Ia-specific input; ablate the reversal to test loss of load-dependent stance burst augmentation.

title: The significance of dynamical architecture for adaptive responses to mechanical loads during rhythmic behavior
notes: Shows that the dynamical architecture of a motor pattern generator determines how it uses sensory feedback: a nominal Aplysia swallowing model tuned near a heteroclinic channel (versus a generic limit cycle) reproduces in vivo load-induced motor changes and the dramatic slowing seen in vitro when proprioceptive feedback is removed, and matches in vivo burst-length distributions better. Argues that limit-cycle CPG models can miss key load-adaptive properties, so architecture choice constrains how sensory feedback shapes rhythm timing.
animal_study: Replicate the regime-classification approach in another rhythmic system: measure burst-length distributions and responses to added load and to graded proprioceptive removal, then test whether the data favor heteroclinic-channel over limit-cycle dynamics as demonstrated for Aplysia in vitro.
robot_sim: Implement two CPG variants that differ only in architecture (limit cycle vs heteroclinic channel) in a neuromechanical simulation with load-dependent sensory input; compare their responses to load perturbations and to sensory ablation, checking for the predicted slowing and burst-length distribution changes.

title: Balance Control Mediated by Vestibular Circuits Directing Limb Extension or Antagonist Muscle Co-activation
notes: Jessell Correspondence a.murray@ucl.ac.uk (A.J.M.), tmj1@columbia.edu (T.M.J.) In Brief Murray et al.

title: Contribution of Cutaneous Inputs From the Hindpaw to the Control of Locomotion. I. Intact Cats
notes: Bilateral hindpaw cutaneous denervation at the ankle in intact cats barely disrupts level treadmill walking but severely impairs ladder and incline walking early on; flexor EMG remains permanently elevated and mediolateral ground reaction forces increase by 200 percent, showing cutaneous feedback matters most for demanding locomotor contexts and that active adaptive mechanisms compensate without fully restoring the control pattern. The companion paper shows these same inputs become critical for foot placement after spinalization.
animal_study: Combine graded cutaneous denervation with spinalization in the same animals to quantify when cutaneous input shifts from contributory to critical for foot placement, and track EMG compensation chronologically to dissect the adaptive mechanisms.
robot_sim: Add foot/ankle cutaneous afferent channels to a walking simulation and ablate them: the model should reproduce near-normal level walking with degraded ladder/incline behavior, persistently elevated flexor drive, and increased mediolateral ground reaction forces.

title: Convergent evolution and locomotion through complex terrain by insects, vertebrates and robots
notes: Argues from convergent evolution that insects and vertebrates independently arrived at similar neural control properties and mechanical schemes for legged locomotion, highlighting leg specialization, body flexion, and complex head-mounted sensing as critical for complex-terrain agility - features most robots of the era lacked. The design-transfer principle is selection rather than copying: pick the properties critical for the target behavior when building a robot.
animal_study: Quantify the convergent properties experimentally, for example measure how restricting body flexion or ablating leg specialization changes complex-terrain traversal in insects, testing whether the convergent features are functionally critical as the convergent-evolution argument predicts.
robot_sim: Build legged-robot models that incrementally add leg specialization, body flexion, and head-region sensing over a homogeneous-leg rigid-body baseline, and compare complex-terrain agility to test which convergent properties carry the performance benefit.

title: Modulation of ipsi- and contralateral reflex responses in unrestrained walking cats
notes: In unrestrained walking cats, cutaneous stimulation evokes phase-modulated responses: two excitatory peaks (about 10 and 25 ms) in flexors that grow toward the end of stance, early inhibition then late excitation (P3, about 35 ms) in extensors when stimuli fall in early stance, and crossed responses in the contralateral limb at 20-25 ms. Concludes the walking cat shows modulation of transmission in a flexor-excitatory/extensor-inhibitory pathway - likely by the flexor part of the spinal locomotor oscillator - rather than strict reflex reversal, plus specialized flexor-inhibitory and extensor-excitatory routes.
animal_study: Record from spinal interneurons during phase-modulated cutaneous reflexes in walking cats to locate where the locomotor oscillator gates transmission, and compare sural versus plantar stimulation sites to map the specialized flexor-inhibitory and extensor-excitatory pathways.
robot_sim: Implement cutaneous reflex pathways with locomotor-phase gating: flexor excitation whose gain peaks at late stance, extensor inhibition during early stance, and crossed extensor/flexor responses; ablating the phase gating tests the oscillator-modulation hypothesis versus fixed reflex reversal.

title: A Dynamic Neural Network Designed Using Analytical Methods Produces Dynamic Control Properties Similar to an Analogous Classical Controller
notes: Shows that analytically designed, biologically constrained neural controllers for bipedal balance can reproduce classical inverted-pendulum control behavior, with each neural parameter correlated to a classical control parameter: varying neural parameters changes system dynamics as classical theory predicts. Establishes a porting recipe from classical control models to compact dynamic neural architectures.
animal_study: Test the parameter-to-stability mappings in human balance experiments: perturb stance and manipulate task demands, then check whether observed adaptation matches the changes predicted when the corresponding neural parameters are varied.
robot_sim: Use the analytical design method to port a classical bipedal balance controller to a neural network in simulation, then ablate or perturb individual neural parameters to verify each reproduces the dynamics change its correlated classical parameter predicts.

title: Spinal control of locomotion--from cat to man.
notes: Review establishing that spinal networks generate the basic locomotor rhythm across vertebrates including man, with limb sensory feedback essential for effective locomotion: sensory regulation reaches motoneurons via reflex pathways that bypass the rhythm generators and also acts on the locomotor networks themselves, controlling phase timing, shaping muscle-activity patterns, adding excitatory drive, and driving long-term adaptation - the basis for treadmill-training rehabilitation after spinal cord injury.
animal_study: In spinalized preparations or spinal-cord-injury patients, dissociate the two sensory routes by stimulating limb afferents during treadmill locomotion and measuring phase-timing versus pattern changes, testing whether reflex-bypass and CPG-directed pathways can be selectively engaged for rehabilitation.
robot_sim: Implement both sensory routes in a locomotion model - direct reflex pathways to motoneurons plus afferent input to the rhythm generator - and ablate each separately to test their predicted contributions to phase timing, pattern shaping, and net excitatory drive.

title: Postural orientation and equilibrium: what do we need to know about neural control of balance to prevent falls?
notes: Frames postural control as two interacting goals - orientation (active alignment of trunk and head to gravity, support surface, and visual surround) and equilibrium (movement strategies stabilizing the center of body mass) - achieved by dynamic sensorimotor processes in which the weighting of somatosensory, vestibular, and visual inputs depends on task goals and context; anticipatory postural adjustments precede voluntary limb movement, and damage to different underlying systems yields context-specific instabilities.
animal_study: Test context-specific instability predictions by selectively disrupting individual sensory systems (visual, vestibular, somatosensory) or CNS subsystems during stance and perturbation tasks, mapping which postural goal and response strategy degrades for each lesion.
robot_sim: Implement a balance controller with task- and context-dependent weighting of somatosensory, vestibular, and visual channels plus anticipatory postural adjustments before limb movements; ablating single channels should reproduce distinct, context-specific instability signatures.

title: Restoring walking after spinal cord injury.
notes: Review of walking restoration after spinal cord injury: treadmill training with partial weight support exploits spinal locomotor networks whose training-induced improvement mechanisms were revealed in animal studies; functional electrical stimulation of nerves and muscles assists stepping; and regeneration strategies promote growth of damaged axons - but no direct spinal-cord treatment is in routine use, so successful protocols will likely combine re-establishing functional connections to spinal networks with task-specific rehabilitation that shapes their motor patterns.

title: Failure of Averaging in the Construction of a Conductance-Based Neuron Model
notes: A conductance-based model built from the mean maximal conductances of a population of equivalent one-spike bursters fires three action potentials per burst instead of one, because the population occupies a highly concave region of parameter space that does not contain its mean - demonstrating that averaging parameters across multiple preparations can fail to characterize a system whose behavior depends on interactions among highly variable components. A core caution for parameterizing neural models from pooled experimental data.
animal_study: Measure maximal-conductance variability across identified neurons in multiple preparations and test whether behavior correlates with parameter covariation across the population rather than with any single-parameter mean, as the concave-parameter-space argument predicts.
robot_sim: When fitting neural or CPG models to multiple experimental recordings, select parameter sets by matching behavior rather than by averaging parameters, and always verify that the mean-parameter model reproduces the target dynamics - an explicit modeling-hygiene rule for database-driven model construction.

title: Spinal reflexes, mechanisms and concepts: from Eccles to Lundberg and beyond.
notes: Historical review of Eccles' intracellular recordings defining five classical spinal reflex systems - recurrent inhibition of motoneurons via motor axon collaterals and Renshaw cells, pathways from muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs, presynaptic inhibition, and the flexor reflex - and of Lundberg's demonstration that spinal interneurons converge segmental sensory afferents with descending pathways, the keystone for modern hypotheses of spinal motor control later tested in behaving animals and non-invasively in humans.
animal_study: Directly record genetically identified spinal interneurons in behaving animals during natural movements to test the functional roles of the Eccles-Lundberg reflex circuits, and examine plasticity of these pathways during motor learning and neurorehabilitation.
robot_sim: Implement the classical circuit library - Renshaw recurrent inhibition, spindle and tendon-organ reflex pathways, presynaptic inhibition, flexor reflex - as separable modules in a spinal network model, ablating each to quantify its contribution to motor output.

title: Functional subdivision of feline spinal interneurons in reflex pathways from group Ib and II muscle afferents; an update.
notes: Reassesses the subdivision of adult mammalian spinal intermediate-zone interneurons and finds no compelling reason to separate those with group Ib input from those co-excited by group II afferents: distributed input patterns, projection targets (ipsilateral, contralateral, bilateral), excitatory versus inhibitory identity, and task-dependent reflex changes during locomotion are all consistent with shared premotor interneurons integrating group I and II signals - prompting the proposed renaming to group I/II interneurons.
animal_study: Record identified intermediate-zone interneurons during locomotion and test whether individual neurons integrate convergent group I and II input with task-dependent output changes, the key prediction of the merged group I/II population proposal.
robot_sim: Replace separate Ib and II reflex channels in a locomotion model with a single premotor interneuron population receiving convergent group I and II input, and test whether the merged population reproduces the task-dependent reflex modulation and reversals seen during locomotion.

title: On the initiation of the swing phase of locomotion in chronic spinal cats.
notes: In chronic spinal cats walking on a treadmill, a limb held by the paw lifts off and rejoins walking once the hip is brought far enough back, at a hip angle very close to that of normal swing initiation, and lift-off also tends to occur at particular contralateral cycle phases. Establishes hip position and contralateral step-cycle phase as two key factors determining swing initiation, i.e., the stance-to-swing transition is regulated by proprioceptive and interlimb signals rather than a fixed internal clock.
animal_study: Block or manipulate hip-joint afferent signals during locomotion in spinal cats and mechanically vary the contralateral cycle phase to dissociate the two swing-initiation factors, testing whether either alone suffices to trigger lift-off.
robot_sim: Implement swing initiation in a walking model as a hip-extension position threshold gated by contralateral cycle phase; ablating the hip-position input should delay or prevent swing onset, reproducing the held-paw behavior.

title: Force-sensitive afferents recruited during stance encode sensory depression in the contralateral swinging limb during locomotion.
notes: Review with new data in the in vitro neonatal rat spinal cord-hindlimb (SCHIP) preparation arguing that contralateral stance-phase force feedback evokes powerful primary afferent depolarization (PAD)-mediated presynaptic inhibition of the swinging limb's own afferents — load in the stance limb sets the sensory gain of the contralateral limb during swing, a mechanism the authors call possibly the most pivotal mechanosensory event of alternating gait. The paper's section 'role of sensory feedback during locomotion' catalogs further afferent rules (sensory timing of flexor drive, load regulation of extensor amplitude) with citations — a rich source for this database's feedback entries.

title: Inhibition and Facilitation of the Spinal Locomotor Central Pattern Generator and Reflex Circuits by Somatosensory Feedback From the Lumbar and Perineal Regions After Spinal Cord Injury.

animal_study: In spinalized cats, stimulate lumbar versus perineal regions during locomotion while recording locomotor output and foot cutaneous reflexes, testing the opposite inhibitory/facilitatory CPG effects and reflex-gain modulation, and probing for pathological loss of functional specificity.
robot_sim: Add region-specific somatosensory gating to a spinal locomotor model: lumbar input inhibits and perineal input facilitates the CPG, with opposite modulation of cutaneous reflex gain; simulating complete spinal-cord injury then tests emergence of maladaptive co-activation of locomotion with other spinal functions.

title: Postnatal Phenotype and Localization of Spinal Cord V1 Derived Interneurons

title: Safe adjustment regions for legged locomotion paths
notes: Integrates footstep-planning foothold evaluation with online touchdown adjustment by computing safe adjustment regions - bounds on how far a step through rough terrain can be modified while remaining collision-free and stably supportable - demonstrated on a prototype humanoid robot.
robot_sim: Add a safe-adjustment-region constraint to a biped walking controller's stepping module so that push-recovery and terrain-driven step modifications stay within collision-free, support-stable bounds.

title: Peripheral proprioceptive modulation in crayfish walking leg by serotonin
notes: Serotonin acts directly and peripherally on crayfish coxo-basal chordotonal organ afferent terminals, dose-dependently boosting primary afferent discharge (maximal near 1 uM, inhibitory at high concentrations in some units), providing a peripheral neuromodulatory route for gain-setting proprioceptive feedback during locomotion without altering central circuitry.
animal_study: Test whether endogenous serotonin reaches the chordotonal organ in vivo during walking, e.g. measure CB CO afferent gain before and after blocking peripheral 5-HT receptors, or correlate 5-HT content in the sensory cells with state-dependent changes in motor reflex gain.
robot_sim: Add a state-dependent gain multiplier on proprioceptive afferent channels (a serotonin-analog neuromodulation knob ranging from facilitation to suppression) and test how reflex gain and locomotor pattern organization change as it is swept.

title: Pseudo-proprioceptive motion feedback by electric stimulation
notes: Electro-tactile sensory substitution can convey lower-limb posture to paraplegic exoskeleton users, matching intact proprioception on hip joint-angle precision and time delay, though not on sensitivity to inertia changes — quantifying how much state information a substitute feedback channel must carry for walking support.
robot_sim: Replace simulated proprioceptive feedback with a quantized, delayed substitute channel (matching the demonstrated precision/delay equivalence but degraded inertia sensitivity) and test locomotion-controller robustness to information-poor feedback.

title: Towards a factored analysis of legged locomotion models
notes: Factorizes the return maps of hybrid legged-locomotion models to obtain an exact algebraic necessary condition for the asymptotic stability of spring-loaded inverted pendulum (SLIP) running across different leg-recirculation strategies, despite the non-integrability of SLIP dynamics — a stability-analysis tool extensible to other legged-locomotion models in robots and animals.
robot_sim: Apply return-map factorization to derive algebraic stability conditions for SLIP-template runners and for CPG or reflex-controlled walkers, using the exact condition as a design check when tuning leg recirculation and stance dynamics.

title: Tuning of neural oscillators for the design of rhythmic motions

robot_sim: Use describing-function algebra to select neural-oscillator parameters (frequency, coupling, gains) for rhythmic joint controllers analytically rather than by simulation sweeps, and verify limit-cycle amplitude and phase against the algebraic predictions in a CPG-driven walker.

robot_sim: Apply output-only simultaneous-perturbation tuning to a neural-oscillator CPG controlling a simulated biped's joints, reproducing learned walking and stepping waveforms as an alternative to gradient-based parameter fitting.

notes: Dissociates load from kinematics in perturbed human walking: adding Lokomat resistance and independently clamping the knee pattern each increase swing-phase quadriceps activity, with the load manipulation contributing more, evidence that load-sensitive feedback rather than just the altered movement pattern drives compensatory swing muscle activity.
animal_study: Replicate the load-versus-length dissociation in an animal model: apply controlled limb loading with kinematics held constant during locomotion in cats or rodents and record swing-phase muscle activity to separate load-sensitive from length-sensitive reflex contributions.
robot_sim: Implement separate force-based (load) and length/velocity-based (stretch) feedback channels onto swing-phase extensor motoneurons; apply simulated resistance and kinematic clamping, then ablate each channel to test their independent contributions.

title: Identified proprioceptive afferents and motor rhythm entrainment in the crayfish walking system
notes: In the crayfish walking leg, the thoraco-coxal muscle receptor organ's two graded nonspiking afferents, phasic T and tonic S, mediate opposing feedback pathways that alternately excite opposite burst phases, so proprioceptor stretch entrains the central rhythm through complete, probabilistic resetting of burst transitions within one or two stimulus cycles.
animal_study: Verify in vivo: record TCMRO afferent activity and leg motor bursts during free walking to confirm that natural stretch timing resets burst transitions as in vitro, and selectively ablate or hyperpolarize the S or T afferent to test the inferred opposing-pathway organization.
robot_sim: Build a two-phase oscillator resettable by graded phasic and tonic afferent channels with opposing effects on burst transitions; test entrainment ranges, coordination ratios (2:1, 1:2, 1:3), and resetting probability as in the crayfish preparation.

title: MPC-based Controller with Terrain Insight for Dynamic Legged Locomotion
notes: A terrain-aware control strategy for dynamic legged locomotion that combines a convolutional-neural-network module evaluating candidate footholds from on-board perception with a model-predictive controller optimizing ground-reaction forces over the chosen contact sequence, demonstrated in HyQReal simulations traversing rough terrain under realistic on-board sensing and computation constraints.
robot_sim: Implement a CNN-based foothold scorer feeding a GRF-optimizing MPC contact sequence for rough-terrain legged locomotion under on-board compute limits, and benchmark against CPG/reflex controllers on the same terrain.

title: Deadbeat control with (almost) no sensing in a hybrid model of legged locomotion
notes: Shows theoretically and in simulation that control laws can be geometrically encoded in the feedforward trajectories of appendages, giving deadbeat stability in hybrid legged models: a simplified vertical hopper rejects ground-height changes without sensing the ground. Cautions that control identified in an existing animal or machine may reside in such geometric stabilization rather than neural or computational feedback.
animal_study: Test the caution in running animals: block distal sensory feedback while systematically varying terrain height and test whether feedforward appendage trajectory shaping alone preserves stability — a positive result would indicate geometric, non-neural stabilization.
robot_sim: Encode a desired control law into the open-loop joint trajectories of a simulated hopper or legged model, remove all feedback loops, and verify deadbeat stability and ground-height rejection as achieved here with little or no sensing.

title: Data driven models of legged locomotion
notes: Reviews Data Driven Floquet Analysis — fitting empirical return maps to the trajectories of rhythmic legged systems — and collects the recent and classical results that justify its use for analyzing legged locomotion where idealized periodicity assumptions fail.
animal_study: Apply DDFA to perturbed walking animals (brief treadmill speed steps or ground-height changes in cats) and test whether the empirically fitted Floquet modes predict recovery trajectories and stability limits.
robot_sim: Fit data-driven Floquet maps to joint-angle cycles from a simulated walker, extract mode structure and stability, and compare with the model's analytic eigenstructure — checking that simulation trajectories support the same empirical analysis as animal data.

animal_study: Test hip afferent priority in a reduced preparation: oscillate the hip in decerebrate cats while eliciting patellar and Achilles reflexes, checking whether hip position similarly gates distal reflexes as in human SCI.
robot_sim: Make knee and ankle reflex gains in a leg model depend on hip angle (larger patellar gain during extension, larger tonic vibration response during flexion); ablate the dependence to test its role in spastic-reflex modulation.

notes: Demonstrates a scalable biologically inspired gait for modular reconfigurable robots in which passively compliant leg attachments and body articulation alone yield a stable dynamic running gait — the first example of dynamic legged locomotion driven only by body articulation (shown in a hexapedal configuration).
robot_sim: Simulate a multi-leg body whose only actuation is trunk articulation with spring-damped compliant legs; verify stable dynamic gaits emerge from mechanical coupling without per-leg control, and map the compliance range over which this holds.

title: Estimation of musculoskeletal models from in situ measurements of muscle action in the rat hindlimb
notes: Computational model study. In many cases these peripheral systems have been shown to simplify neural control or make natural behaviors more efficient (Nishikawa et al., 2007; Pfeifer et al., 2007; Valero-Cuevas et al., 2007b).

title: Motion Control of a Robot Fish Based on CPG
notes: Robot fish driven by a CPG of four neural oscillators with sensory feedback from three infrared sensors and a gyro; two feedback strategies mapped to CPG model parameters control pitching and turning respectively, with simulations validating rhythm generation for pectoral-fin and tail-flapping locomotion. An early engineering demonstration that modulating CPG parameters with simple exteroceptive and proprioceptive signals suffices for posture and heading control in swimming.
robot_sim: Reproduce the two feedback strategies in a simulated swimmer: map obstacle-detection (infrared-analog) and posture (gyro-analog) signals onto CPG parameters for turning and pitching, then ablate each feedback path to quantify the open- versus closed-loop difference in obstacle avoidance and attitude stability.

notes: Mice lacking Wt1 in neurons run slower with decreased stride frequency and increased stride length, show altered fore-hindlimb coordination accompanied by loss of contralateral spinal projections, and display arrhythmic reduced-frequency motor output as neonates — tying a Wt1-expressing dI6 subpopulation to left-right coordination circuitry assembly.
animal_study: Test whether the coordination deficits are afferent-dependent: run Wt1 mutants on a treadmill with perturbations, or evoke locomotion pharmacologically in neonatal spinal cords while recording ventral roots, separating circuit miswiring from sensory reweighting.
robot_sim: Reduce contralateral commissural projection weights in a bilateral CPG to mimic Wt1 loss; check for slower cadence, longer strides, degraded interlimb coordination, and arrhythmic motor output.

title: Neuromusculoskeletal Modeling for the Adaptive Control of Posture During Locomotion
Synchronization of coupled neural oscillators with heterogeneous delays
notes: Analysis of two coupled excitable neural systems showing that heterogeneous delays in mutual and self-coupling select different regimes of synchronized oscillation of variable period, with bursting-like dynamics emerging from two competing timescales — conduction-delay structure, not only coupling strength, governs oscillator synchronization. Directly relevant to commissural coupling in CPGs, where crossing delays are non-negligible.
animal_study: Test whether conduction-delay manipulation shifts synchronization of biological coupled oscillators: e.g., in vitro spinal hemicord pairs with imposed variations in crossing delay, measuring whether synchronized frequency and phase relations change as the model predicts.
robot_sim: Implement two coupled half-centers with explicit heterogeneous conduction delays in mutual and self-connections; sweep delays to map synchronization regimes and test whether commissural delay tuning alone switches coordination mode or oscillation period.

title: Characterization of WT1-expressing interneurons and investigation of their role in locomotion
notes: Thesis using a newly developed upright in vitro mouse spinal cord preparation that keeps the locomotor CPG intact to record WT1-expressing ventral interneurons during fictive locomotion: WT1+ cells are inhibitory, project mainly commissural axons, and regulate left-right alternation; viral tracing of their upstream synaptic partners constrains the network structure of the locomotor CPG.
animal_study: The preparation is itself the animal study; follow-ons include silencing or ablating WT1+ cells in vivo during locomotion to test necessity for left-right alternation, and activating them to test sufficiency.
robot_sim: Implement an inhibitory, commissurally projecting interneuron population (WT1-analog) as the left-right alternation pathway in a bilateral CPG; ablating it should push the model toward synchronous gaits, a loss-of-function test of interleg coordination design.

title: Reactive posture behaviors for stable legged locomotion over steep inclines and large obstacles
notes: Reactive posture behaviors let the hexapod robot LAURON cross large obstacles and steep slopes with no knowledge of the environment, aided by the increased kinematic adaptability of a bio-inspired fourth rotational leg joint — demonstrating that layered reactive behaviors can substitute for terrain models in rough-terrain walking.
robot_sim: Implement layered reactive posture behaviors (leg stance adaptation, posture correction) with no environment model on a simulated hexapod with a fourth leg rotation joint; stress-test against the same obstacle and slope envelope to find the limits of purely reactive control.

title: A Piecewise-Linear Approximation of the Canonical Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum Model of Legged Locomotion
notes: A piecewise-linear approximation of the spring-loaded inverted pendulum — whose only nonlinearity is the stance-flight switching event — reproduces the bifurcation structure and parametric sensitivities of the nonlinear SLIP model across parameter space while providing closed-form stance trajectories and touchdown-to-touchdown stride maps that compute far faster than numerical integration.
robot_sim: Use the closed-form piecewise-linear stride map as a fast analytical plant for gait planning and stability analysis in legged-robot controllers, validating bifurcation fidelity against numerically integrated SLIP.

title: The Bcm rule allows a spinal cord model to learn rhythmic movements
notes: Demonstrates that a monolayer spinal-circuitry model with Bienenstock-Cooper-Munro plasticity can learn rhythmic alternating movements of pendulum plants without rhythm-generating neurons or genetically defined connectivity — a learning-based alternative or supplement to hard-wired CPG models that explains how a common spinal circuit plan could adapt to the different biomechanics and locomotion patterns of different species.
animal_study: Test in vitro whether alternating rhythmic output can be trained in otherwise quiescent spinal circuits by patterned paired stimulation consistent with BCM plasticity, with deafferented controls bounding how much is learned versus hard-wired.
robot_sim: Implement a monolayer neuron network with BCM synaptic plasticity driving pendulum or joint plants and test whether rhythmic alternating control emerges without oscillator units; comparing against fixed-weight CPG controllers isolates the contribution of the learning rule.

title: Synchronization dynamics of two coupled neural oscillators receiving shared and unshared noisy stimuli
notes: For two weakly coupled neural oscillators, shared (correlated) noise can induce bistability between synchronous and anti-phase states even when anti-phase is the only stable state without noise; an asymptotic Fokker-Planck reduction (rho(0)) is far cheaper than Monte-Carlo or 2D solvers and accurately predicts a synaptically coupled Morris-Lecar system.
animal_study: Apply shared versus independent stochastic stimulation to two biological rhythm-generating circuits (e.g., isolated hemicords) and test whether correlated input alone produces bistable synchronous/anti-phase locking, as the theory predicts.
robot_sim: Inject correlated sensory noise into two weakly coupled half-centre oscillators to verify noise-induced bistability between synchrony and anti-phase, and use the rho(0) phase reduction in place of Monte-Carlo simulation for parameter sweeps.

title: Learning to stop: a unifying principle for legged locomotion in varying environments
notes: Proposes 'learning to stop' — endowing locomotion controllers with the ability to halt safely — as a unifying principle for locomotion in varying environments: a deep deterministic policy gradient agent with the stop capability transfers controllers from water to land quickly and safely, plausibly modeling how locomotion strategies crossed the water-to-land transition.
animal_study: In an amphibious animal model, quantify stopping behavior and recovery from destabilization during initial water-to-land locomotor experience to test whether stopping competence accompanies newly transferred locomotion strategies, as the learning-to-stop hypothesis predicts.
robot_sim: Train DDPG locomotion controllers with and without an explicit stop action in water and land simulations and compare transfer success, training safety, and recovery from destabilization across environments.

title: Proprioceptive postural control of a musculoskeletal model against horizontal disturbances

title: Spinal Cord Circuits: Models and Reality
Stimulation of the Spinal Cord for the Control of Walking
