animal_study: Measure cost of transport and preferred speed of animals or humans walking on low-friction versus normal surfaces, testing the counterintuitive prediction that tolerated slippage can improve energetic efficiency.
robot_sim: Implement the two-mass torque-actuated SLIP with Coulomb friction; sweep friction to locate stick-slip periodic solutions and test whether slippage regimes lower cost of transport and raise average speed.

title: Motor module activation sequence and topography in the spinal cord during air-stepping in human: Insights into the traveling wave in spinal locomotor circuits.
notes: During human air-stepping, which removes foot-contact interactions, four NMF-extracted motor modules activated sequentially, with reconstructed motoneuron clusters progressing from rostral to caudal spinal regions from initial flexion to the last extension phase — evidence for rostrocaudally traveling waves in human locomotor spinal circuits, resolving the rostral propagation shift previously observed at foot contact during walking.
animal_study: Record spinal or muscle activity in an animal model during air-stepping versus grounded stepping to separate the CPG-internal rostrocaudal wave sequence from sensory effects of foot contact.
robot_sim: Implement a rostrocaudally sequenced motor-module CPG (a traveling wave over distributed MN pools) and reproduce the module activation order from initial flexion to late extension during unloaded stepping, then add ground contact to test waveform modulation.

title: Enhancing postural stability in a musculoskeletal hopping robot through stretch reflex application on biarticular thigh muscles
notes: Guided by this physiological principle, this study aims to enhance the postural stability of a hopping robot through the emulation of this human mechanism.

title: On All Fours: A 3D Framework to Study Closed-loop Control of Quadrupedal Mouse Locomotion
notes: Proof-of-concept 3D closed-loop neuromechanical mouse: four limb rhythm generators drive pattern-formation circuits generating muscle synergies, with commissural and long-propriospinal interlimb coordination and spindle/Golgi/cutaneous feedback terminating in the RG, PF, and motoneuron layers; evolution-optimized flat-ground walking collapses with acute feedback removal.

title: Incidence and Cost of Serious Fall-Related Injuries in Nursing Homes
notes: Over a 3-year period, there were 2,400 admissions to VHA hospitals for FRI, with 55.4% hip fractures and10.1% intracranial injuries, with an average cost of US$23,723 per admission.

title: Hummingbird flight
notes: Many different species of plants show a vernalization response — do they all use the same mechanism to control this response?.

title: Modular organization of the multipartite central pattern generator for turtle rostral scratch: knee-related interneurons during deletions
notes: Single-unit interneuron recordings during knee-related deletions in turtle rostral scratch show that knee-extensor and knee-flexor interneurons occupy modules separate from the hip-extensor and hip-flexor modules, establishing at the single-unit level that the limb CPG is multipartite, organized per joint and function rather than as unitary flexor and extensor halves.
animal_study: Test the multipartite organization causally in other vertebrates: silence or lesion the identified knee-related interneuron modules during rostral scratch and assay whether knee bursts drop out in deletions while hip rhythm persists, converting the single-unit correlational evidence into a causal claim.
robot_sim: Implement a multipartite CPG with separate hip and knee flexor/extensor modules per joint; reproduce deletions by transiently silencing individual modules and verify that other modules continue bursting, then compare against a classical bipartite half-center controller.

title: Stepping responses to treadmill perturbations vary with severity of motor deficits in human SCI
notes: Split-belt treadmill perturbations during human stepping show that stopping one belt in midstance triggers an unnecessary swing in most walkers, with the likelihood dropping as SCI severity increases, while belt acceleration or deceleration during stance advances or delays swing onset — evidence for interdependent central and sensory drive in stepping control that degrades with injury severity.

title: Constancy and Variability in the Output of a Central Pattern Generator
notes: In the leech heartbeat CPG, animal-to-animal variation in the absolute and even relative strengths of the four premotor inputs does not correlate strongly with output phase; functional output is preserved because multiple, phase-diverse inputs dilute the influence of any single connection, implying each animal reaches a unique parameter solution for the same motor pattern.
animal_study: Measure synaptic strengths and motor-output phases across many individuals of the same CPG preparation and correlate parameter variation with functional output to test compensatory and degeneracy mechanisms.
robot_sim: Randomize synaptic strengths across simulated individuals of a CPG-driven network and test whether input-number and phase-diversity degeneracy preserves functional output; ablate single inputs to quantify their diluted influence.

title: Synaptic connectivity amongst components of the locomotor central pattern generator
notes: Synaptic connectivity amongst locomotor CPG components — updates the wiring diagram of rhythm and pattern elements with paired-recording data.

title: Parametric resonance for vibration energy harvesting with design techniques to passively reduce the initiation threshold amplitude
notes: Experimental results of the parametric resonant harvesters with these additional enabling designs demonstrated up to an order of magnitude lower initiation threshold than otherwise, while attaining a much higher power peak than direct resonance.

notes: Controller for continuous-wave peristaltic locomotion in a worm-like robot; traveling-wave body actuation with local reflexes.

title: Vision can recalibrate the vestibular reafference signal used to re-establish postural equilibrium following a platform perturbation

title: Balancing of humanoid robot using contact force/moment control by task-oriented whole body control framework
notes: The proposed approach in this paper is to maintain balance of torque-controlled robots by controlling contact force and moment using whole-body control framework with hierar- chical structure.

title: Lumbar V3 interneurons provide direct excitatory synaptic input onto thoracic sympathetic preganglionic neurons, linking locomotor, and autonomic spinal systems
notes: Lumbar locomotor V3 interneurons provide direct, somatotopically organized excitatory synaptic input to thoracic sympathetic preganglionic neurons (8-20% of their glutamatergic input), where optical activation evokes prolonged depolarizations or action potentials — an intraspinal route coupling locomotor activation to autonomic recruitment without supraspinal mediation.
animal_study: Silence or ablate lumbar V3 interneurons during locomotion while recording sympathetic outflow and autonomic effectors, to test whether this intraspinal pathway is necessary for movement-coupled autonomic activation.
robot_sim: Add a propriospinal excitatory branch from lumbar CPG modules to an autonomic controller layer in a neuromechanical model and ablate it to quantify the loss of locomotion-driven autonomic entrainment.

title: Slack-based tunable damping leads to a trade-off between robustness and efficiency in legged locomotion
notes: Motivated by the concept of an adaptive mechanism triggering an immediate response, we developed a tunable physical damper system.

title: Proprioceptive Stimulation Added to a Walking Self-Avatar Enhances the Illusory Perception of Walking in Static Participants
notes: Adding gait-patterned lower-limb muscle vibration to a first-person walking avatar increased static participants' sense of agency and illusory perception of walking; only realistic, temporally aligned proprioceptive stimulation produced anteroposterior center-of-pressure sway matching the avatar's gait cadence — congruent proprioceptive input alone can evoke motor correlates of gait.

title: Design of a Canine Inspired Quadruped Robot as a Platform for Synthetic Neural Network Control
notes: Computational model study. DoggyDeux features a fully 3D printed frame, 24 braided pneumatic actuators (BPAs) that drive four 3-DOF limbs in an- tagonistic extensor-flexor pairs, and an electrical system that allows it to respond to commands from a SNN comprised of central pattern genera- tors (CPGs).

title: Computing Motion Dependent Afferent Activity During Cat Locomotion Using a Forward Dynamics Musculoskeletal Model
Left-right locomotor coordination in human neonates
notes: In 46 stepping neonates, interlimb coordination is variable (including 2:1 locking episodes and activity deletions on a blocked side), hip-position effects are strictly ipsilateral (backward hip position engaging hip flexors, flexed position engaging hip extensors), sudden posterior release of a blocked limb elicits immediate swing initiation, and extensor muscles show load responses at midstance, indicating neonatal networks with independent per-limb pattern generators and load and hip-position feedback but incomplete sensory modulation relative to mature locomotion.
animal_study: Apply matched limb-blocking stepping protocols across immature animals of different species to determine which interlimb coordination features mature after birth and how closely neonatal networks match spinal mammalian preparations.
robot_sim: Model per-limb flexor and extensor pattern generators with hip-position and load feedback but weak interlimb coupling; reproduce 2:1 coordination episodes and activity deletions, then strengthen coupling parameters toward mature alternation.

title: Integrating Non-spiking Interneurons in Spiking Neural Networks
notes: Additionally, we show that non-spiking neurons can effecti vely manipulate post-synaptic spiking neurons.

title: Unusual Quadrupedal Locomotion in Rat during Recovery from Lumbar Spinal Blockade of 5-HT7 Receptors.
notes: Spinal 5-HT7 receptor blockade (not 5-HT2A) in adult rats reorganizes recovery quadrupedal locomotion into a transiently stable 2:1 forelimb-to-hindlimb stepping pattern, implicating lamina VII 5-HT7-expressing interneurons with ascending projections in setting fore-hindlimb coupling.
animal_study: Silence or ablate lamina VII 5-HT7-positive ascending interneurons, or apply SB269970 selectively rostral versus caudal to a spinal transection, to localize where the 2FL-1HL coupling is generated and confirm the receptor-subclass specificity.
robot_sim: Model fore-hindlimb coupling through an ascending serotonergic-modulated interneuron path between hindlimb and forelimb CPGs; removing the 5-HT7-like gain should lock the network into a 2:1 forelimb-to-hindlimb pattern.

title: Control of Cat Walking and Paw-Shake by a Multifunctional Central Pattern Generator
notes: A single half-center CPG model with two coexisting activity regimes — fast ~10 Hz paw-shake and slow ~2 Hz walking — drives a neuromechanical cat-hindlimb model to produce either behavior when regime-appropriate spinal synaptic weights are selected; paw skin afferent input is proposed as the trigger for selecting both the CPG regime and the spinal circuitry.

title: Control strategies of 3-cell Central Pattern Generator via global stimuli
notes: We show how, with a suitable combination of short and weak global inhibitory and excitatory stimuli over the whole network, we can switch between different stable bursting patterns in small neuron networks (in our case a 3-neuron network).

notes: Computational model study. Recently, numerous molecular and genetic approaches have been proposed for investigating the CPG mechanisms.

notes: In this study, we present the design and preliminary testing of two distinct mechanism modules that are novel for passive prosthetic knee applications: the stability module and the damping module.

title: A postural control model incorporating multisensory inputs for maintaining a musculoskeletal model in a stance posture
notes: Computational model study. In this study, our aim was to develop a stance postural control model including a neural controller with feed-forward controlandsensoryfeedbackcontrolbasedonvisual,vestibular,andproprioceptivesomatosensory feedback inputs.

title: Diversified physiological sensory input connectivity questions the existence of distinct classes of spinal interneurons
notes:
The spinal cord is engaged in all forms of motor performance but its functions are
far from understood. Because network connectivity defines function, we
explored the connectivity of muscular, tendon, and tactile sensory inputs among
a wide population of spinal interneurons in the lower cervical segments. Using
low noise intracellular whole cell recordings in the decerebrated, non-anesthetized cat in vivo, we could define mono-, di-, and trisynaptic inputs as well as
the weights of each input. Whereas each neuron had a highly specific input, and
each indirect input could moreover be explained by inputs in other recorded neurons, we unexpectedly also found the input connectivity of the spinal interneuron
population to form a continuum. Our data hence contrasts with the currently
widespread notion of distinct classes of interneurons. We argue that this suggested diversified physiological connectivity, which likely requires a major
component of circuitry learning, implies a more flexible functionality.

title: The Motor Circuit
notes: Reviews the C. elegans ventral nerve cord motor circuit — its architecture, development, fate-specifying genes, and models of locomotor control — and identifies surprising structural and developmental similarities between the nematode and vertebrate axial nerve cords, speculating that conserved transcription factor families shaped the evolution of both motor circuits.
animal_study: Test the speculated conservation: knock down or knock out the conserved transcription factor families in a vertebrate preparation and assay whether motor neuron fate specification and circuit organization parallel the nematode sequence.

title: Feedback design for multi-contact push recovery via LMI approximation of the Piecewise-Affine Quadratic Regulator
notes: Computational model study. We show that we can embed a quadratic objective in the SDP, designing a controller approximating the Piecewise-Afﬁne Quadratic Reg- ulator .

title: How deletions in a model could help explain deletions in the laboratory.
notes: No usable abstract in the record (publisher full-text holder only). From the title alone: a commentary proposing that deleting components in a computational locomotor model could help explain 'deletions' observed in laboratory data.

title: Force and motion management in legged locomotion
notes: Legged locomotion over uneven terrain is statically indeterminate and unstable under position-velocity control; directly controlling actuator forces — as in multi-fingered grasping, under an assumption of zero horizontal foot interaction forces — removes the stability problem at moderate computational cost.
robot_sim: Swap joint position-velocity control for direct force control in a legged simulator on uneven terrain and verify the predicted stability improvement and computational savings under the zero-horizontal-foot-interaction assumption.

title: The functional diversity of spinal interneurons and locomotor control
Postural control and adaptation are influenced by preceding postural challenges

notes: A robotic-fish controller in which sensory feedback reshapes CPG coupling topology and parameters online — with a finite-state machine selecting among swimming gaits — improves maneuverability and adaptability in simulation and underwater tests, an engineering demonstration of feedback-driven CPG reconfiguration for multimodal locomotion.
robot_sim: Implement a CPG whose coupling forms and control parameters are shaped online by sensory feedback under finite-state gait selection; test multimodal gait switching and adaptation to environmental change against fixed-coupling CPGs.

notes: Here we exam- ine one ostensibly simple case of the NACA 0012 aerofoil and make careful comparison between the technical literature, and new experiments and com- putations.

title: Flexor and Extensor Ankle Afferents Broadly Innervate Locomotor Spinal Shox2 Neurons and Induce Similar Effects in Neonatal Mice.
notes: Shox2 CPG neurons in neonatal mice are broadly innervated by both flexor- and extensor-related ankle afferents, which evoke similar currents without the expected functional antagonism; stimulation of either resets ongoing fictive locomotion to flexion, so low-threshold proprioceptive input reinforces sensory perturbation of both the rhythm and patterning layers.
animal_study: Stimulate identified afferent classes (Ia, II, Ib) during fictive locomotion in Shox2 reporter mice while recording Shox2 neurons, or delete Shox2 subpopulations, to test their necessity for afferent phase resetting.
robot_sim: Add broad convergent low-threshold proprioceptive input onto both rhythm and patterning layers so that flexor- or extensor-related activation resets the CPG to flexion; ablate the Shox2-analog population to test loss of afferent resetting.

title: Biologically inspired gait transition control for a quadruped walking robot
notes: Computational model study. A Two- Way oscillator coupling has been used for modeling the CPG.

title: Symmetry in legged locomotion: a new method for designing stable periodic gaits
Systematic generation of biophysically detailed models with generalization capability for non-spiking neurons
notes: Computational model study. Such neurons have been found in a large variety of nervous tis- sues in both vertebrate and invertebrate species, and have been proven to play a central role in neuronal information processing.

title: An Intersegmental Neuronal Architecture for Spinal Wave Propagation under Deletions
notes: During cat scratching, traveling electrical waves along the spinal cord persist through extensor-burst deletions that leave the cycle unaltered, whereas deletions that perturb the cycle coincide with loss of the traveling wave; numerical simulations of an asymmetric two-layer CPG distributed longitudinally along the cord reproduce both the sinusoidal waves and both deletion classes, supporting a longitudinal chain organization of CPG networks.
animal_study: Record global spinal activity during scratching with targeted microlesions or microstimulation of intersegmental connections to test whether removing specific longitudinal links eliminates the traveling wave while sparing local rhythm, directly probing the two-layer chain architecture.
robot_sim: Implement a longitudinally distributed asymmetric two-layer CPG and perturb individual unit oscillators to reproduce the deletion dichotomy (cycle-preserving versus cycle-perturbing deletions); use it to calibrate intersegmental coupling in multi-segment walkers.

title: Optimal exploitation of natural dynamics in legged locomotion
Sensory Modulation of Locomotor-Like Membrane Oscillations in Hb9-Expressing Interneurons
notes: In isolated neonatal mouse spinal cords, low-threshold afferents produce short-latency monosynaptic excitatory responses in most Hb9 interneurons, with VGLUT1- and parvalbumin-immunoreactive afferent contacts on somata and dendrites, and afferent input resets neurochemically induced locomotor-like rhythms: flexor-related afferent stimulation during the flexor phase delays subsequent cycle onsets while extensor-related stimulation prolongs cycle period two- to threefold, with Hb9 IN oscillations remaining phase-locked to motor bursts throughout. Hb9 INs are therefore sensorimotor interneurons positioned to regulate the pattern of locomotor rhythms.
animal_study: Ablate or silence Hb9 interneurons, for example by targeted lesion in Hb9:eGFP mice, during drug-induced locomotor-like activity to test whether afferent-induced cycle resetting is lost while the rhythm itself persists.
robot_sim: Add an Hb9 interneuron layer receiving monosynaptic afferent input and phase-locked to motor bursts in a CPG model; ablating the layer should remove the afferent phase-resetting effects on cycle timing without abolishing rhythmicity.

title: Chapter 10--a hierarchical perspective on rhythm generation for locomotor control.
notes: Implemented Brown's half-center CPG concept as reciprocally organized integrators whose parameters were optimized to satisfy the biomechanical requirements of overground locomotion, finding that the control signal driving each limb's CPG corresponds to the desired speed of forward progression; supports a scheme in which descending and sensory feedback inputs combine into a high-level command that sets forward velocity, with steering generated by differential speed commands to different limbs.
animal_study: Record spinal network activity across locomotor speeds in reduced preparations to test whether the combined descending-sensory drive corresponds to desired forward speed, and during turning to test for differential speed-command input across limbs.
robot_sim: Drive each limb's half-center CPG with a speed-command signal and implement steering as differential speed commands across limbs, with phase-duration characteristics matched by optimization; removing the sensory component of the combined drive should degrade velocity regulation.

title: Different Motor Neuron Spike Patterns Produce Contractions With Very Similar Rises in Graded Slow Muscles
notes: A consequence of spike-number dependency is that brief changes in spike frequency do not alter contraction slope and we show here that extensor motor neuron bursts with different spike patterns give rise to contractions with very similar contraction rises.

title: An adaptive locomotion controller for a hexapod robot: CPG, kinematics and force feedback
notes: Computational model study. To tackle this challenge, a central pattern generator (CPG)-based locomotion control methodology is proposed, integrated with a contact force feedback function.

title: Distinguishing subtypes of spinal locomotor neurons to inform circuit function and dysfunction
notes: Perspective on linking spinal interneuron identity to locomotor function: molecular identification of broad interneuronal classes advanced the field, and adding location, electrophysiological properties, and connectivity sharpens function assignment, but some functional populations - notably rhythm-generating neurons - lack clear identifiers, and experience-dependent plasticity plus spinal cord injury complicate subtype definitions, making multimodal classification necessary for understanding circuit function and dysfunction.
animal_study: Combine gene profiling with location, electrophysiology, connectivity, and perturbation recordings in behaving animals to assign function to molecularly defined spinal subtypes, and search for markers that uniquely identify rhythm-generating neurons.
robot_sim: Build locomotor network models whose unit classes are constrained by the multimodal classifiers, including an as-yet-unidentified rhythm-generating population; deleting specific classified subtypes in the model tests predicted functional deficits and can guide which neurons to target for identification.

title: Sensory Feedback in the Control of Posture and Locomotion
notes: Book chapter synthesizing sensory control of posture and locomotion in arthropods and vertebrates through classical feedback-control theory, arguing that experimental paradigms, reduced animal preparations, and neuromechanical modeling must be combined to understand postural control, which in both groups maintains a body-configuration set point (a set of joint angles keeping the body above the feet) during standing, locomotion, and other movements, and resists sudden perturbations.
animal_study: Apply perturbation paradigms in reduced arthropod and vertebrate preparations to isolate individual sensory feedback loops, testing the control-theoretic prediction that each loop defends a defined body-configuration variable against disturbances.
robot_sim: Build posture controllers for simulated walkers per the chapter's framework - body-configuration set points defended by sensory feedback loops - and ablate loops individually to compare predicted versus resulting postural deficits in arthropod- and vertebrate-style morphologies.

title: Proprioceptive feedback contributes to the adaptation toward an economical gait pattern
notes: Disrupting plantarflexor proprioception with noisy Achilles tendon vibration left level walking largely unchanged but slowed adaptation to a 2.5% incline — shorter stride periods and redistributed medial gastrocnemius activity (reduced mid-stance, increased late-stance) persisted for 2-3 minutes before converging, and uphill metabolic cost rose — indicating proprioceptive feedback is needed to rapidly identify low-cost muscle activation patterns.
animal_study: Replicate in an animal model: apply tendon vibration or selectively silence ankle extensor proprioception during locomotion on changing inclines and measure adaptation rate, redistribution of muscle activation, and metabolic cost.
robot_sim: Add a proprioception-dependent adaptation layer to a neuromuscular gait model that searches for economical activation patterns; ablate the proprioceptive input and reproduce the delayed adaptation and elevated cost under a mechanical demand change.

title: A physical model of sensorimotor interactions during locomotion.
notes: A bipedal robot with strap actuators, Golgi-tendon-organ-like strap load sensors, and a spiking half-center CPG with phase-modulated reflexes walks with the cycle entrained to body dynamics, and the CPG stabilizes gait against perturbations beyond a purely reflexive controller — a physical test of CPG-reflex synergy benchmarked against human walking trajectories.
animal_study: Compare perturbation recovery in intact versus deafferented walking animals to quantify the stabilizing contribution the robot attributes to the CPG — the reflex-only versus CPG+reflex contrast predicts smaller recovery margins after deafferentation.
robot_sim: Replicate in simulation: half-center CPG plus phase-modulated reflexes with Ib strap-force feedback on a biped; ablate the CPG to leave reflex-only control and quantify the stability loss against matched perturbations.

title: Use of Visual and Proprioceptive Feedback to Improve Gait Speed and Spatiotemporal Symmetry Following Chronic Stroke: A Case Series
notes: In two chronic stroke patients, 18 sessions of treadmill gait training augmented with continuous real-time visual feedback (immersive virtual environment) and proprioceptive feedback (dual-belt treadmill) improved gait speed and spatiotemporal symmetry beyond levels previously reported, with each patient improving the symmetry dimension they trained (step-length versus stance-time). Shows augmented sensory channels can drive relearning of gait symmetry after stroke.
animal_study: Test combined visual and proprioceptive symmetry feedback in a larger stroke cohort with retention follow-up, and dissociate the two channels to determine whether proprioceptive (split-belt driven) or visual augmentation drives the symmetry gains.
robot_sim: Model gait adaptation as an external feedback loop: real-time symmetry error signals delivered through visual and proprioceptive channels drive step-to-step correction of a neuromuscular gait controller, reproducing the differential improvement in the trained symmetry dimension.

title: Organization of common synaptic drive to motoneurones during fictive locomotion in the spinal cat
notes: Common drive to motoneurones during fictive locomotion is organized in low-frequency coherent components that group muscles into functional synergies; locomotor drive is shared rather than muscle-specific.

title: Dynamic spinal reflex adaptation during locomotor adaptation
notes: Provides direct evidence that spinal reflexes can be modulated on demand and unilaterally during split-belt locomotor adaptation in healthy adults, and proposes reflex-gain modulation itself as a candidate mechanism for the adaptation of gait asymmetry.
animal_study: A split-belt adaptation protocol with serial reflex testing, plus reversible blockade of the tested reflex arc, in an animal model would establish whether unilateral reflex modulation is necessary for adapting step asymmetry or merely correlates with it.
robot_sim: Implement reflex pathways with side-specific, adaptable gains in a bilateral walker and test whether modulating reflex gain alone (holding CPG drive fixed) reduces gait asymmetry during split-belt perturbations.

title: Shining light into the black box of spinal locomotor networks
notes: Reviews how new genetic approaches that identify and manipulate specific interneuron classes are opening the mammalian locomotor CPG 'black box' that had previously been probed only through input-output manipulation, critically discussing these techniques in relation to current models of network function.

robot_sim: Populate a simulated locomotor network with genetically identified interneuron classes as distinct node types (rhythmogenic vs pattern-organizing populations) and match model ablation phenotypes to the genetic loss-of-function data reviewed.

title: A controller perspective on biological gait control: Reflexes and central pattern generators
notes: Reviews the neural control of gait from a control-engineering perspective and argues the biological CPG is asymmetric: the rhythm generator drives the flexor half in feedforward fashion while the extensor half operates in feedback mode, gated by external inputs such as ground contact — an architecture with direct implications for how biped robots should couple CPGs to contact sensing.

title: Stabilization of posture by precision touch of the index finger with rigid and flexible filaments
notes: Our findings indicate that: (1) stimula- tion of a small number of receptors in the fingertip is ad- equate to allow stabilization of sway, (2) fingertip force levels as low as 5–10 g provide some stabilization, (3) contact with a stationary spatial referent is most...

title: The possibility of phase-dependent monosynaptic and polysynaptic la excitation to homonymous motoneurones during fictive locomotion
Physiologically based controller for generating overground locomotion using functional electrical stimulation.
notes: In spinal cats stepping via functional electrical stimulation, an intrinsically timed controller achieves overground stepping more easily (lower sensitivity to initial stimulation parameters) but cannot compensate walkway resistance or muscle fatigue, while a sensory-driven controller that switches between unloaded flexion and loaded extension phases adapts to loading — motivating a combined controller that runs on intrinsic timing but resets phase from sensory signals.
animal_study: Compare intrinsically timed, sensory-driven, and combined FES controllers across repeated sessions in instrumented spinal cats, quantifying load-bearing stepping and adaptation to induced muscle fatigue.
robot_sim: Implement a fixed-timing CPG with load-based sensory phase resetting (combined controller) in a neuromuscular biped; ablating the sensory reset should cause failures under fatigue-like actuator force decay and changing walkway resistance, reproducing the timed controller's limitation.

title: Flush Air Data Sensing for Soaring-Capable UAVs
notes: Introduction S mall Uninhabited Ferial Vehicles t uavsux with a wingspan of + meters or less and mass under 1 kgx have tremendous potential in military and civilian applicationsz These aircraft are usually handylaunchable with small operational footprintsx but this small size also limits payload...

title: Vibration receptive sensilla on the wing margins of the silkworm moth Bombyx mori
notes: Each kind of sensillum is specialized both morphologically and physiologically for detecting its own speciﬁc sensory quality.

title: Distinct roles of spinal commissural interneurons in transmission of contralateral sensory information
notes: Two genetically distinct commissural interneuron populations carry crossed reflexes in mice: the exclusively excitatory V3 CINs directly mediate excitatory crossed reflexes and are essential for inhibitory ones, while the mixed V0 CINs are not directly involved in either but downregulate inhibitory crossed reflexes - linking genetically identified locomotor commissural populations to contralateral sensory transmission.
animal_study: Selectively activate or silence V0 versus V3 commissural interneurons while recording contralateral reflex EMG to establish necessity and sufficiency for the excitatory and inhibitory crossed reflex components.
robot_sim: Implement left-right coupling with two commissural populations - a direct excitatory V3-analog pathway plus a V0-analog modulatory population scaling inhibitory crossed pathways - and ablate each to test interlimb reflex coordination.

title: A walking robot called human: lessons to be learned from neural control of locomotion.
notes: Distills cat and human locomotion into design principles for walking robots: control at three levels (actuator/motoneuron, whole-limb flexion-extension oscillators with mutual inhibition, interlimb coordination), with the most essential feedback at the limb level, where activation of the extensor part of the limb oscillator must be triggered by feedback signalling onset of loading via limb load sensors, and flexor activation must require unloading below a threshold plus a hip position within the normal end-of-stance range.
animal_study: Independently manipulate limb loading and hip position during stepping in decerebrate cats to isolate each factor's causal contribution to the flexion-versus-extension decision, as the proposed control rules predict.
robot_sim: Implement the three-level architecture with limb-level decision rules: extensor oscillator activation on limb loading (load-sensor threshold) and flexor initiation gated on unloading below threshold together with hip position in the end-of-stance range; ablate each rule and quantify gait robustness loss.

title: Kinematic primitives for walking and trotting gaits of a quadruped robot with compliant legs
notes: This revealed that kinematic patterns resulting from feed-forward control had a lower complexity (in-air stepping, 2–3 primitives) than kinematic patterns from on-ground locomotion (4 primitives), although both experiments applied identical motor patterns.

title: Hip and ankle responses for reactive balance emerge from varying priorities to reduce effort and kinematic excursion: A simulation study
notes: Computational model study. Similar to prior studies using torque- driven models, we investigated how movement patterns during a reactive balance response are affected by high-level task goals (e.g., reducing center-of-mass movement, maintaining vertical trunk orientation, and minimizing effort).

title: Rare phenomena of central rhythm and pattern generation in a case of complete spinal cord injury
notes: In a complete thoracic spinal cord injury, self-sustained spinal myoclonus proved to tap spinal circuits that generate muscle spasms rather than a locomotor CPG, whereas epidural electrical stimulation produced flexor-extensor and left-right alternating patterns with spontaneous motor deletions - preserved cycle frequency and period when rhythmicity resumed - previously reported only in animals, supporting a separation between rhythm generation and pattern formation in the human lumbar cord.
animal_study: Compare EES-induced motor deletions and myoclonus mechanisms in spinal cord injury subjects with analogous animal fictive locomotion recordings to establish the cross-species homology of rhythm-versus-pattern separation.
robot_sim: Separate rhythm and pattern modules in a CPG controller: transiently silence the rhythm kernel while the pattern-formation circuitry retains its phase relationships, reproducing motor deletions with preserved cycle period upon resumption.

title: Proprioceptive feedback reinforces centrally generated stepping patterns in the cockroach
notes: In the cockroach, which can generate coordinated leg patterns without sensory feedback, imposed transient and periodic movements of a single intact leg phase-dependently modified phase relationships among other legs' segmental oscillators: front-leg feedback is weaker but more phase-precise than hind-leg feedback, selectively strengthening the inherent rhythmic pattern while modulating local perturbations — proprioception reinforces rather than replaces the central pattern.
animal_study: Identify and selectively ablate the leg proprioceptors mediating the effect, then impose single-leg transient and periodic movements to quantify how front- versus hind-leg feedback strength and phase precision shape inter-leg coordination.
robot_sim: Implement hexapod segmental oscillators with leg-local proprioceptive feedback that adjusts inter-oscillator coupling, giving front legs lower gain but tighter phase precision; ablate the feedback to test degradation of pattern robustness to local perturbations.

title: The central pattern generator for forelimb locomotion in the cat.
notes: In decerebrate cats with fictive forelimb locomotion evoked by repetitive cervical lateral funiculus stimulation, the shortest descending pathway to cervical motoneurons via the CPG is disynaptic, and the intercalated interneurons are proposed to form mutually exciting, reverberating circuits that constitute the CPG itself. Disynaptic, trisynaptic, and polysynaptic PSPs in motoneurons are phase-related to the rhythm with reciprocal modulation between extensor and flexor responses, indicating interactions between the mediating pathways.
animal_study: Record and stimulus-identify cervical interneurons intercalated in the cervical lateral funiculus pathways during fictive forelimb locomotion, testing whether the disynaptic interneurons mutually excite one another and sustain reverberating activity consistent with CPG membership.
robot_sim: Implement the forelimb CPG as a reverberating, mutually excitatory interneuron loop driven disynaptically from a descending command; ablating the mutual excitation should collapse the rhythm and its phase-locked PSP modulation.

title: Phase shift between joint rotation and actuation reflects dominant forces and predicts muscle activation patterns
notes: This study proposes a nondimensional number that relates these four forces: the phase shift (ϕ) between the displacement of the limb and the actuator force that moves it.

title: Structural Model of the Muscle Spindle
notes: Computational model study. — A model of the muscle spindle was developed based on its anatomical structure.

title: Loading the Limb During Rhythmic Leg Movements Lengthens the Duration of Both Flexion and Extension in Human Infants
notes: In rhythmic leg movements of human infants, load-related feedback prolongs whichever phase is more loaded: stepping on a treadmill, kicking against a plate, and kicking in sitting lengthen extension, whereas air-stepping with ankle weights lengthens flexion, and infants exerting lower forces show shorter extensor durations. Manipulating weight-bearing during stepping confirms the effect, showing that the degree of loading directly and incrementally affects the duration of the loaded phase.
animal_study: In animal rhythmic-movement preparations (for example spinal air-stepping versus supported stance), manipulate limb loading with weights or foot-plate contact to test whether the more loaded phase lengthens in a graded manner as in infants.
robot_sim: Implement load-dependent phase-duration modulation, in which the more loaded phase of the step cycle lengthens incrementally, in a stepping network; ablate the load input to test phase-duration changes.

title: Resonance tuning in a neuro-musculo-skeletal model of the forearm
notes:
Cited  by Geyer and Herr, 2010.
In rhythmic movements, humans activate their muscles in a robust and energy efficient way. These activation patterns are oscillatory and seem to originate from neural networks in the spinal cord, called central pattern generators (CPGs). Evidence for the existence of CPGs was found for instance in lampreys, cats and rats. There are indications that CPGs exist in humans as well, but this is not proven yet. Energy efficiency is achieved by resonance tuning: the central nervous system is able to tune into the resonance frequency of the limb, which is determined by the local reflex gains. The goal of this study is to investigate if the existence of a CPG in the human spine can explain the resonance tuning behavior, observed in human rhythmic limb movement. A neuro-musculo-skeletal model of the forearm is proposed, in which a CPG is organized in parallel to the local reflexloop. The afferent and efferent connections to the CPG are based on clues about the organization of the CPG, found in literature. The model is kept as simple as possible (i.e., lumped muscle models, groups of neurons are lumped into half-centers, simple reflex model), but incorporates enough of the essential dynamics to explain behavior—such as resonance tuning—in a qualitative way. Resonance tuning is achieved above, at and below the endogenous frequency of the CPG in a highly non-linear neuro- musculo-skeletal model. title: Maintenance of Lateral Stability During Standing and Walking in the Cat
notes: Lateral perturbations in the cat recruit context-specific postural mechanisms: during standing, corrective redistribution of muscle activity between symmetrical limbs (contralateral hindlimb extensor excitation with ipsilateral inhibition); during walking, a corrective lateral step whose direction depends on push timing relative to the step cycle and whose EMG signature is marked hip abductor and adductor reprogramming — reconfiguring the base of support rather than redistributing activity.
animal_study: Apply phase-controlled lateral pushes before and after deafferentation or spinal transection to determine which afferents encode the lateral perturbation and whether the corrective-step reprogramming is spinal.
robot_sim: Implement phase-dependent lateral-perturbation correction in a legged model — standing mode redistributes extensor activity across limbs, walking mode triggers a corrective lateral step via step-cycle-gated hip abductor/adductor modulation — and test recovery against push timing.

title: Practice-related improvements in posture control differ between young and older adults exposed to continuous, variable amplitude oscillations of the support surface
notes: This study provides important insight into the ability of older adults to demonstrate longer-term improvements in postural regulation.

title: Spinal Sensorimotor Circuits Play a Prominent Role in Hindlimb Locomotor Recovery after Staggered Thoracic Lateral Hemisections but Cannot Restore Posture and Interlimb Coordination during Quadrupedal Locomotion in Adult Cats
notes: Staggered thoracic lateral hemisections in cats: hindlimb locomotion recovers spontaneously but forelimb–hindlimb coordination degrades into weaker 2:1 patterns, left–right stance/swing asymmetries appear then reverse after the second hemisection, and posture plus interlimb coordination remain impaired — lumbar sensorimotor circuits carry hindlimb recovery but not supraspinal-dependent coordination.

title: Modulation of phase durations, phase variations, and temporal coordination of the four limbs during quadrupedal split-belt locomotion in intact adult cats
notes:
During experiments, EMG and bilateral video recordings were made during
treadmill locomotion from 0.1 to 0.4 m/s in 0.05 m/s increments.
Cycle and stance durations significantly decreased with increasing
speed, whereas swing duration remained unaffected. Extensor burst
duration significantly decreased with increasing speed, whereas sartorius burst duration remained unchanged. Stride length, step length,
and the relative distance of the paw at stance offset significantly
increased with increasing speed, whereas the relative distance at
stance onset and both the temporal and spatial phasing between
hindlimbs were unaffected. Both temporal and spatial step-to-step
left-right asymmetry decreased with increasing speed. Therefore, the
spinal cord is capable of adjusting both temporal and spatial parameters during treadmill locomotion, and it is responsible, at least in part,
for the step-to-step variability in left-right symmetry observed at slow
speeds.

title: A versatile and efficient pattern generator for generalized legged locomotion
notes: A model-predictive walking pattern generator computes a dynamically consistent center-of-mass trajectory and angular momentum for arbitrary contact configurations (uneven, sloppy, slippery terrain, closed grippers) fast enough for online use, integrated with an acyclic contact planner and second-order hierarchical inverse kinematics; demonstrated on HRP-2 for long-step walking and staircase climbing with handrail support.
robot_sim: Implement a fast MPC-based center-of-mass and angular-momentum pattern generator over arbitrary planned contact sequences as a biomechanical baseline layer for biped controllers, and compare its robustness on uneven or sparse contacts with CPG-reflex approaches.

title: Proprioceptive Feedback and Preferred Patterns of Human Movement
notes: Hypothesis paper proposing that the stereotyped movement patterns humans prefer during cyclical tasks are identified via proprioceptive feedback reporting body mechanics, rather than solely by minimizing metabolic energy expenditure — preferred movement patterns may depend on body mechanics and be partially dependent on proprioceptive feedback.
animal_study: Remove proprioceptive feedback during cyclical tasks (ischemic block or tendon vibration) and test whether the selected preferred movement pattern shifts toward patterns predicted by body mechanics alone.
robot_sim: Implement an optimizer that selects movement patterns using simulated proprioceptive signals (length, force) as objective variables rather than metabolic cost alone; compare predicted preferred patterns with and without the feedback term.

title: Phase-dependent transmission in the excitatory propriospinal reflex pathway from forelimb afferents to lumbar motoneurones during fictive locomotion
notes: During fictive locomotion in high spinal paralyzed cats, forelimb nerve stimulation evokes EPSPs in hindlimb extensor motoneurons only during extension and in flexor motoneurons only during flexion, establishing that transmission in the descending excitatory propriospinal reflex pathway is cyclically gated at the lumbar level by the locomotor rhythm.
animal_study: Test the lumbar phase-gating by stimulating forelimb nerves at defined cycle phases while recording lumbar interneurons and motoneurons in reduced preparations, or section the descending propriospinal pathways to assess loss of forelimb-hindlimb coordination during overground locomotion.
robot_sim: Add forelimb-to-hindlimb excitatory propriospinal coupling to a quadruped CPG, gated by lumbar phase (excitation reaching extensor motoneurons during extension and flexor motoneurons during flexion); removing the phase gate should scramble interlimb coordination.

title: Multiple chaotic central pattern generators with learning for legged locomotion and malfunction compensation
Spinal control of locomotion before and after spinal cord injury
notes: Sampling the full speed range exposes hidden structure in rat spinal locomotor control: intact rats express a speed-dependent continuum from alternating gaits (walk, trot) to non-alternating ones (canter, gallop, half-bound, bound); lateral thoracic hemisection removes only the fastest non-alternating gaits while preserving interlimb coordination on the injured side, and moderate contusion lowers maximal speed, eliminates all non-alternating gaits, and yields novel alternating gaits - signatures of weakened fore-hind propriospinal coupling with preserved left-right alternation control.
animal_study: Combine wide-speed gait testing with selective silencing of long propriospinal neurons to causally link fore-hind coupling strength to the expression of non-alternating gaits after injury.
robot_sim: Model interlimb coordination as speed-dependent coupled oscillators with a long-coupling analog between fore and hind rhythm units; ablating that coupling should eliminate bound and gallop modes while sparing alternating gaits and left-right alternation.

title: Ionic conductances underlying the activity of interneurons that control heartbeat in the medicinal leech
notes: Hyperpolari- zation of HN neurons with injected currents revealed a time- dependent change in membrane potential, whereby initial maximum hyperpolarization was followed by a “sag” in po- tential towards more depolarized values.

title: Interlimb coordination during fictive locomotion in the thalamic cat.
notes: Interlimb coordination during fictive locomotion in the thalamic cat persists without phasic sensory feedback, demonstrating central interlimb coupling that sensory input can then modulate.

title: Electrophysiological and Pharmacological Properties of Locomotor Activity-Related Neurons in cfos-EGFP Mice
notes: In this study, we demonstrate a new way of identifying neurons active in locomotion.

title: Decoding the mechanisms of gait generation in salamanders by combining neurobiology, modeling and robotics
notes: Salamanders exhibit both swimming and stepping gaits and is faced with the problem of producing efficient propulsive forces using the same musculo-skeletal system in two environments with significant physical differences in density, viscosity and gravitational load. Authors' approach is based on a combination of neurophysiological experiments, numerical modeling at different levels of abstraction, and robotic validation using an amphibious salamander-like robot.

title: Adaptive hindlimb split-belt treadmill walking in rats by controlling basic muscle activation patterns via phase resetting
notes: Forward dynamic simulation with a neuromusculoskeletal rat model supports resetting the onset timings of a few basic muscle-activation patterns by leg sensory feedback — especially hip-flexor extension — as the mechanism adapting hindlimb walking to split-belt treadmill conditions.

title: The mammalian spinal commissural system: properties and functions.
notes: Review of mammalian spinal commissural interneurons — heterogeneous cells definable by gray-matter location, axonal projections and targets, neurotransmitter phenotype, activation properties, and embryological origin — whose crossed projections coordinate left-right motor activity in locomotion and posture; their roles in grasping, reaching, and bimanual control remain poorly understood, especially in the cervical cord of primates including humans, and they are implicated in restoration of function after spinal injury and stroke.
animal_study: Record identified commissural interneuron classes during locomotion and reaching in animals, including primate cervical cord to fill the reviewed gap, and selectively silence individual classes to test their necessity for left-right alternation and posture.
robot_sim: Implement multiple heterogeneous commissural interneuron classes with distinct signs, targets, and drive dependencies in a bilateral CPG; ablating each class should produce distinct left-right coordination deficits, and graded lesions can model post-injury recovery.

title: Altered Gravity Highlights Central Pattern Generator Mechanisms
notes: Parabolic-flight experiments show the period of human voluntary rhythmic arm movements shortens systematically with increasing gravity, while in weightlessness it depends more on task instruction, matching a computational model of a CPG coupled to a simple pendulum in which the CPG exploits near-resonant driving - evidence that CPG mechanisms flexibly entrain rhythmic movement to changing gravitational and mechanical contexts.
animal_study: In animals, manipulate effective gravity or limb loading (added mass or buoyancy) and test whether rhythmic-movement frequency tracks the shifted mechanical resonance as the CPG-pendulum account predicts.
robot_sim: Couple an oscillator or CPG to a pendular limb plant under variable gravity and loading; verify frequency adaptation toward resonance and the loss of resonance-locking in weightlessness when the pattern is purely command-driven; ablate the coupling to test the mechanism.

title: Integration of posture and rhythmic motion controls in quadrupedal dynamic walking using phase modulations based on leg loading/unloading
Locomotor pattern generation and descending control: a historical perspective
notes: Historical review of vertebrate locomotor control organizing a century of work into three interacting systems: spinal central pattern generators produce the basic rhythm, brainstem descending inputs initiate, maintain, and stop locomotion while controlling speed and direction, and sensory inputs adapt the locomotor program to environmental conditions.
animal_study: Use the review's framework to design experiments dissociating descending from sensory control - for example brainstem-evoked locomotion with progressive deafferentation - in a chosen vertebrate preparation.
robot_sim: Structure a locomotor controller as a spinal CPG plus brainstem-analog descending commands (start, stop, speed, direction) plus sensory adaptation loops, and test that removing each layer reproduces its predicted functional loss.

title: Combining series elastic actuation and magneto-rheological damping for the control of agile locomotion
notes: This paper describes the locomotion control of a leg prototype, designed and developed to make a quadruped walk dynamically while exhibiting compliant interaction with the environment.

title: Quadrupedal galloping control for a wide range of speed via vertical impulse scaling
notes: The bilateral feedback system shows robustness to inertial variations and to external disturbances with the proposed human-in-the-loop control strategy offering valuable insight for future work.

title: Segmental patterns of vestibular-mediated synaptic inputs to axial and limb motoneurons in the neonatal mouse assessed by optical recording
notes: Optical recording reveals segmental patterns of vestibular-mediated synaptic input to axial and limb motoneurons in the neonatal mouse; vestibular influence on the cord is segmentally organized — strong on axial, weaker on limb.

title: Common and distinct muscle synergies during level and slope locomotion in the cat.
notes: Cat downslope walking's atypical EMG (silent one-joint hip extensors, stance-related flexor bursts) shares the majority of its burst groups and muscle synergies with level and upslope walking, and slope changes swing/stance phase durations but not cycle duration — consistent with one shared CPG whose output is reshaped by somatosensory and supraspinal inputs rather than task-specific circuit reconfiguration.
animal_study: Record hindlimb EMG across slope and split-belt transitions and test whether synergy vectors remain fixed while activation timing scales, or deafferent the preparation to isolate the CPG contribution to the shared synergies.
robot_sim: Drive a fixed muscle-synergy output layer from a single CPG whose phase-duration scaling reproduces slope-dependent EMG; verify the model predicts the downslope silent hip extensors and stance flexor bursts without changing synergy vectors.

title: A neuro-mechanical model of legged locomotion: single leg control
notes: Neuro-mechanical single-leg model uniting CPG and peripheral feedback: a neural phase generator gates fast sensory feedback pathways according to the current step phase and filters inconsistent afferent input, while sensory signals both act directly on the motor system and entrain the phase generator; with elastic actuators the model steps stably over a large velocity range.
animal_study: Apply standardized perturbations at defined step phases in an animal walking preparation and measure reflex compensation, testing the predicted phase-appropriate gating of feedback by cycle state.
robot_sim: Implement a neural phase generator that gates fast feedback per step phase, with elastic actuators and sensory entrainment of the generator; ablate the gating so feedback is always on, and test for over-control and instability.

title: Adaptation after vastus lateralis denervation in rats demonstrates neural regulation of joint stresses and strains
notes: In this study, we hypothesized that the central nervous system (CNS) chooses muscle activations to avoid excessive joint stresses and strains.

title: Walking with perturbations: a guide for biped humans and robots
notes: Review of bipedal walking for biologists and roboticists: argues CPG function is fundamentally asymmetric (the flexor half more tightly coupled to the rhythm generator), catalogs phase-dependent trip-recovery strategies (elevating and lowering) and the comparison of expected versus actual feedback for stepping into a hole, and tracks emerging robotics implementations including learning to fall safely and split-belt disturbances.

title: On the central pattern generator for the basic breathing rhythmicity
notes: On the central pattern generator for the basic breathing rhythmicity.

title: A Silicon Central Pattern Generator Controls Locomotion in Vivo
notes: First in vivo demonstration of a neuromorphic silicon CPG replacing central nervous system function: a chip of ten integrate-and-fire silicon neurons with 190 programmable synapses drove the motor output of a paralyzed animal to walk a three-meter platform in real time, under closed-loop control using sensory feedback recorded from the animal's legs. Establishes that compact neuromorphic hardware with biological-style sensory feedback can suffice for locomotor pattern generation in a living preparation.
animal_study: The paradigm itself seeds animal studies: run the paralyzed-animal preparation with the silicon CPG open-loop versus closed-loop (leg sensory feedback on/off) and across different synaptic configurations to identify which circuit properties and feedback channels are necessary for overground walking.
robot_sim: Emulate the chip architecture in software (ten integrate-and-fire neurons, arbitrary programmable connectivity, tonic bias, external inputs closed-loop with leg sensory signals) and ablate the sensory feedback path to quantify its contribution to walking stability.

title: Motor cortical regulation of sparse synergies provides a framework for the flexible control of precision walking
notes: Motor cortex regulates sparse synergies during precision walking; cortical control selects and modulates a small set of muscle synergies rather than individual muscles, a framework for goal-dependent gait modification.

title: Mechanical effort predicts the selection of ankle over hip strategies in nonstepping postural responses
notes: Computational model study. First pub- lished August 3, 2016; doi:10.1152/jn.00127.2016.—Experimental studies have shown that a continuum of ankle and hip strategies is used to restore posture following an external perturbation.

title: Sex comparison of extensibility, passive, and active stiffness of the knee flexors
notes: Males show less extensibility and greater active and passive knee-flexor stiffness than females, measured by final knee position in active extension, the slope of the passive moment-angle curve, and damping of imposed vibratory motion under 10 percent body-mass loading; the sex differences may be functions of greater male mass and height, with relevance to higher female anterior cruciate ligament injury rates.
robot_sim: Use the measured passive and active knee-flexor stiffness values (and their sex differences) as joint-level stiffness parameters in a neuromuscular knee model, testing whether stiffness differences alone - without altered reflex gains - change joint stability margins.

title: Central drive and proprioceptive control of antennal movements in the walking stick insect
notes: Stick insect antennal control separates two mechanisms: inter-joint coordination persists after ablating joint proprioceptors, but the working ranges of the scape-pedicel and head-scape joints are set by dorsal antennal hair fields, whose ablation shifts or expands specific joint ranges. De-cerebrated animals walk without antennal movements while pharmacologically induced rhythmic antennal motion persists, and the authors conclude that the activating synaptic drive to the antennal networks resides in the brain rather than the suboesophageal ganglion.
animal_study: Ablate individual antennal hair fields and measure joint working-range shifts during walking to map each field's control range, and test sufficiency by selectively stimulating individual hair-field afferents while recording antennal motor neurons.
robot_sim: Implement joint working-range limitation driven by mechanosensory hair-field-analog feedback on each antennal or limb joint; ablating the range-limiting sensory input should expand joint ranges while inter-joint phasing persists, testing the separation of coordination from range control.

notes: Review of comparative anatomy quadruped robots animals:. To gain a deeper understanding of the source of this versatility in animals and apply the principles of their body plans to robotics, the authors, who work in the robotics and anatomy fields, jointly review and com- pare the essential body structure differences between quadruped...

title: An analysis of the sources of musculoskeletal system impedance
notes: Computational model study. It is shown that impedance modulation occurs automatically as a function of the specific operating ranges utilized during a given task by each of four different muscle-joint mechanical relations.

title: Symbiotic electroneural and musculoskeletal framework to encode proprioception via neurostimulation: ProprioStim
notes: Computational model study. We demonstrated its feasibility through non-invasive stimulation on seven healthy subjects comparing it with standard linear charge encoding.

title: Dynamic response of human muscle spindle afferents to stretch during voluntary contraction
notes: This study was conducted to investigate the basic pattern of dynamic and static fusimotor actions on human muscle spindles.

title: Autonomous gait transition and galloping over unperceived obstacles of a quadruped robot with CPG modulated by vestibular feedback
notes: Review of autonomous gait transition galloping over unperceived obstacles. We conclude that CPGs modulated by vestibular feedback is eﬀec- tive and practical as a gait generator for bio-inspired robots that are expected to have both the abilities of “speed-based autonomous gait transition” and “autonomous robust running”.

title: Motor control of an insect leg during level and incline walking
notes: Here, we studied these parameters in hindlegs of stick insects ( Carausius morosus ) during level and uphill/downhill (±45 deg) walking, using a combination of electromyography, 3D motion capture and ground reaction force measurements.

title: The capsular ligaments provide more hip rotational restraint than the acetabular labrum and the ligamentum teres
notes: In cadaveric hips under functional load, each capsular ligament (iliofemoral medial and lateral arms, pubofemoral, ischiofemoral) acts as the primary rotational restraint somewhere within the full range of motion, the ligamentum teres acts as a secondary restraint in high flexion, adduction and external rotation, and the iliofemoral lateral arm and ischiofemoral ligaments are primary restraints in about two-thirds of the positions tested, quantifying the passive soft-tissue contribution to hip rotational stability.
robot_sim: Use the measured capsular-ligament restraint contributions as position-dependent passive hip rotational stiffness and limits in musculoskeletal or robotic models of the lower limb.

title: BoxyBot: a swimming and crawling fish robot controlled by a central pattern generator
notes: Computational model study. title: Sensorimotor Recalibration Depends on Attribution of Sensory Prediction Errors to Internal Causes
notes: Here, we investigated the recalibration of internal predictions about the sensory consequences of one’s actions.

title: Motor control by precisely timed spike patterns
notes: Review of motor control precisely timed spike patterns. Computational model study. Although traditional theories assume that this information is conveyed by the total number of spikes fired within a specified time interval (spike rate), recent stud- ies have shown that additional information is carried by the milli- second-scale timing patterns of action potentials (spike timing).

title: Maneuvers during legged locomotion
notes: Running turns in bipeds are constrained by matching body rotation to movement direction: humans generate large braking forces to prevent over-rotation whereas ostriches obtain appropriate rotation from lateral force alone (aided by greater rotational inertia relative to body mass), humans stabilize orientation within the theoretical two-step minimum, and horizontal-plane leg forces follow spring-mass behavior — so passive dynamic stabilization contributes to maneuver stability.
animal_study: Record 3D kinetics and kinematics of turning in bipedal species spanning rotational-inertia ratios to test the rotation-matching model's prediction that braking requirements scale with rotational inertia relative to body mass.
robot_sim: Implement a biped with horizontal-plane spring-mass legs and a rotation-matching turn controller; verify that fore-aft braking against over-rotation emerges and that increasing rotational inertia removes the braking requirement, reproducing the human-versus-ostrich contrast.

title: Central pattern generators in the turtle spinal cord: selection among the forms of motor behaviors.
notes: The turtle spinal cord contains separate CPGs for three forms of scratch, two forms of swim, and one flexion reflex, with multisecond motor memories, interneurons partially shared across behaviors (enabling motor pattern blends) alongside behavior-specific cells, and deletion analysis supporting unit burst generators organized per degree-of-freedom direction (hip-flexor, hip-extensor, knee-flexor, etc.) - an organizational complexity the classic flexor/extensor half-center scheme cannot capture.
animal_study: Apply simultaneous dual-behavior stimuli to test the blending mechanism predicted by partially shared interneurons; record single neurons across spontaneous deletions to further test unit-burst-generator organization.
robot_sim: Implement the CPG as unit burst generators per joint direction under a selection layer combining shared and behavior-specific interneurons, and reproduce motor pattern blends and deletions as signatures of that organization.

title: Functional muscle synergies constrain force production during postural tasks.
notes: Computational model study. We recently demonstrated that a set of ﬁve functional muscle synergies were sufﬁcient to characterize both hindlimb muscle activity and active forces during automatic postural responses in cats standing at multiple postural conﬁgurations.

title: Multisensory Feedback Can Enhance Embodiment Within an Enriched Virtual Walking Scenario
notes: Congruent vestibular and proprioceptive feedback (motion platform plus lower-limb tendon vibration) during immersive virtual walking raises subjective embodiment and presence and elevates galvanic skin response and respiration rate relative to vision alone, showing that multisensory afferent congruence drives the embodied walking experience.

title: Internal models and neural computation in the vestibular system
notes: Review of internal models neural computation vestibular. Computational model study. Recent studies have shed new insights into important organizational principles that closely resemble those proposed for other sensorimotor systems, where their neural basis has often been more difﬁcult to identify.

title: A fundamental mechanism of legged locomotion with hip torque and leg damping
notes: Computational model study. These results provide a more clear understanding of the hip-torque-and-leg-damping mechanism of legged locomotion, and extend existing theory of legged locomotion towards a greater understanding of robustly stable locomotion.

title: An electronic implementation for Morris–Lecar neuron model
Integrate-and-fire neurons with threshold noise: A tractable model of how interspike interval correlations affect neuronal signal transmission
notes: Computational model study. We demonstrate that negative correlations in the baseline activity can lead to enhanced information transfer of a weak signal by means of noise shaping of the background noise spectrum.

title: Functionally complex muscles of the cat hindlimb. I. Patterns of activation across sartorius.
notes: During sixteen horizontal platform-translation directions in the standing cat, the three neuromuscular compartments of biceps femoris are activated non-homogeneously, with petal-shaped EMG tuning curves rotating progressively counterclockwise from anterior (hip-extensor-like) through middle to posterior (knee-flexor-like) compartments; the active region moves continuously across anterior and middle compartments with a discontinuity at the middle-posterior border, and functional units do not match the anatomical compartments exactly.
animal_study: Block individual nerve branches or stimulate compartment-specific afferents during directional postural perturbations to test whether the compartment-specific tuning curves reflect segmental afferent organization.
robot_sim: Represent multi-compartment muscles with direction-tuned regional activations (rotated tuning curves per compartment) instead of one activation per muscle, and test improvements in directional postural-response control.

title: Recent Insights into the Rhythmogenic Core of the Locomotor CPG.
notes: Review of the rhythmogenic core of the mammalian locomotor CPG: genetic approaches have identified spinal interneuron populations and their roles in stepping, but the identity and interconnection of the rhythm-generating neurons themselves remain undeciphered; compiles the properties expected of rhythmogenic neurons and the candidate genetically defined classes.
animal_study: Silence candidate rhythmogenic interneuron classes during fictive locomotion and test whether rhythm (as opposed to pattern) collapses, using the review's compiled feature list of rhythm-generating neurons as selection criteria.
robot_sim: Construct a CPG whose rhythmogenic kernel exhibits the expected rhythm-neuron features alongside separate pattern circuitry; ablate candidate kernel classes to test which removal stops rhythm generation while leaving patterning intact.

title: Optimization of Muscle Activity for Task-Level Goals Predicts Complex Changes in Limb Forces across Biomechanical Contexts
notes: Computational model study. In an unrestrained balance task in cats, we demonstrate that achieving task-level constraints center of mass forces and moments while minimizing control effort predicts detailed patterns of muscle activity and ground reaction forces in an anatomically-realistic musculoskeletal model.

title: Asymmetric Operation of the Locomotor Central Pattern Generator in the Neonatal Mouse Spinal Cord
notes: Continuous conductance measurements from neonatal mouse motoneurones during locomotor-like activity show push-pull CPG operation (alternating excitatory and inhibitory conductances with inhibitory predominance, most pronounced in extensors), sharper phase tuning of flexor-related than extensor-related synaptic drives, and rostral-versus-caudal segmental differences - evidence for reciprocally coupled but differently composed flexor and extensor modules in a multilayered, distributed premotor network, preserved across frequencies and drug combinations.
animal_study: Test the rostral/caudal CPG asymmetry with segment-specific recordings or lesions of the isolated cord, and verify the extensor-dominant inhibition with identified premotor interneurone recordings during locomotor-like activity.
robot_sim: Implement premotor modules as reciprocally coupled flexor and extensor half-centers with unequal phase-tuning sharpness, inhibition-dominant extensor drive, and rostral/caudal parameter differences, then compare generated motoneurone conductance profiles with the extracted ones.

title: Models of Postural Control: Shared Variance in Joint and COM Motions
notes: Computational model study. The CCA was performed as a function of established models of postural control that varied in their joint degrees of freedom (DOF), namely, an inverted pendulum ankle model (2DOF), ankle-hip model (4DOF), ankle-knee-hip model (5DOF), and ankle-knee-hip-neck model (7DOF).

title: Recent advances in evolutionary and bio-inspired adaptive robotics: Exploiting embodied dynamics
notes: Argues through four case studies that adaptive behavior is best obtained by exploiting embodied dynamics rather than suppressing them: evolved analog electronic controllers act as robot controllers, insect-inspired navigation builds on innate behaviors, neuromechanical chaos powers a goal-driven search for robust motor behaviors with neural-oscillator architectures, and evolved dynamical controllers yield agile flapping flight robust to wind gusts.
animal_study: For the navigation case: manipulate the visual information supplied by innate behaviors in insect experiments to test the claim that rapid route learning depends on navigation-specific visual information exploited by those innate behaviors.
robot_sim: Adopt the neuromechanical-chaos result: use neural-oscillator controllers whose chaotic dynamics power a goal-driven search for motor behaviors, testing whether robust locomotion emerges by exploiting rather than damping body-level chaos.

title: A mechanism for sensory re-weighting in postural control
notes: Computational model study. A key ﬁnding of human balance experiments has been that the integration of sensory information utilized for postural control appears to be dynamically regulated to adapt to changing environmental conditions and the available sensory information, a process referred to as ‘‘sensory re-weighting.’’ We propose a...

title: Forelimb muscle activity during equine locomotion
notes: Computational model study. The patterns of net muscular torques developed over one gait cycle have been calculated for a wide variety of species using measurements of joint kinematics and ground reaction forces (Clayton et al., 2000; Colborne et al., 1997; Dogan et al., 1991; Fowler et al., 1993;...

title: Processing of Horizontal Optic Flow in Three Visual Interneurons of the Drosophila Brain
notes: First whole-cell recordings of Drosophila horizontal-system cells (HSN, HSE, HSS): direction-selective tuning to large-field horizontal motion consistent with the correlation-type motion-detection model, with extensive ipsilateral coupling explaining sensitivity to both ipsi- and contralateral motion — the circuit basis for optomotor behavior.

title: Complete dynamical analysis of a neuron model
